title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第六十 循吏
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第六十 循吏 Volume 70 Biographies 60: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十循吏

translations.literal: Biography 60: Virtuous Officials
translations.idiomatic: the 60th year of Biography — Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 吉翰杜驥申恬杜慧度阮長之甄法崇傅琰虞願王洪范沈瑀范述曾孫謙何遠郭祖深

translations.literal: Ji Han, Du Ji, Shen Tian, Du Huidu, Ruan Changzhi, Zhen Fachong, Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Wang Hong, Fan Shenyao, Sun Qian, He Yuan, Guo Zushen
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, Du Ji, Shen Tian, Du Huidu, Ruan Changzhi, Zhen Fachong, Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Wang Hong, Fan Shenyao, Sun Qian, He Yuan, and Guo Zushen

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣帝以為「政平訟理，其惟良二千石乎？」。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xuan of Han said, "When government is level and lawsuits are settled, is it not the good administrators of the two-thousand-dan rank?"
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Xuan of Han remarked, "When the administration is fair and litigation is properly resolved, could anything matter more than capable district governors?"

sentences.zh: 前史亦云，今之郡守，古之諸侯也。

translations.literal: The earlier histories also say that today's commandery governors are the feudal lords of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories likewise observe that the commandery governors of today are the feudal lords of old.

sentences.zh: 故長吏之職，號曰親人。

translations.literal: Therefore the office of the chief administrator is called "one who is close to the people."
translations.idiomatic: That is why the chief magistrate's post is styled "kinsman to the people."

sentences.zh: 至於道德齊禮，移風易俗，未有不由之矣。

translations.literal: As for aligning conduct with virtue and rites, and transforming customs and changing popular habits, nothing has ever been achieved without them.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in harmonizing morals with ritual or in reshaping customs and altering popular ways, nothing has ever been accomplished without them.

sentences.zh: 宋武起自匹庶，知人事艱難，及登庸作宰，留心吏職。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song rose from commoner ranks, knew the hardships of human affairs, and once he ascended to office and became chief minister, he paid attention to the duties of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song had risen from the common people and knew life's hardships; once he took power as chief minister, he kept a close eye on official administration.

sentences.zh: 而王略外舉，未遑內務，奉師之費，日耗千金。

translations.literal: Yet with royal strategy directed outward, he had no leisure for internal affairs; the cost of maintaining the army consumed a thousand gold pieces each day.
translations.idiomatic: But with imperial strategy turned outward, he had little time for domestic governance, and the expense of keeping armies in the field drained a thousand gold pieces every day.

sentences.zh: 播茲寬簡，雖所未暇，而黜己屏欲，以儉禦身，左右無幸謁之私，閨房無文綺之飾。

translations.literal: Though he had no time to spread such leniency and simplicity, he restrained himself and barred his desires, governing his person through frugality; those at his side had no private access through favor, and the inner quarters had no patterned-silk adornment.
translations.idiomatic: Though he could not yet extend such leniency and simplicity throughout the realm, he reined himself in and shut out desire, governing his own person through frugality; no favorite at court enjoyed private access, and the inner apartments held no brocade finery.

sentences.zh: 故能戎車歲駕，邦甸不擾。

translations.literal: Therefore he could send war chariots forth year after year without disturbing the domains of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he could march armies year after year without unsettling the realm.

sentences.zh: 文帝幼而寬仁，入纂大業，及難興陝服，六戎薄伐，興師命將，動在濟時。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was from youth generous and humane; he entered to succeed the great enterprise, and when difficulties arose in the Shaan region and the six Rong pressed in with raids, he raised armies and appointed generals, each move aimed at saving the age.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had been gentle and humane from childhood; when he came to the throne and troubles flared in the Shaan region with the six Rong raiding the borders, he raised armies and appointed commanders, every move calculated to rescue the times.

sentences.zh: 費由府實，事無外擾。

translations.literal: Expenses came from the treasury's substance, and affairs were not disturbed from without.
translations.idiomatic: Costs were met from the treasury's own resources, and the realm suffered no outside disruption.

sentences.zh: 自此方內晏安，甿庶蕃息，奉上供徭，止於歲賦，晨出暮歸，自事而已。

translations.literal: From this time the realm within the four seas was tranquil and secure; the common people multiplied; what they rendered to the court in labor and levies stopped at the annual tax; they went out at dawn and returned at dusk, attending only to their own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the empire within the four seas knew peace; the common people multiplied; what they owed the court in labor and levies was limited to the annual tax; they left at dawn and came home at dusk, minding only their own work.

sentences.zh: 守宰之職以六期為斷，雖沒世不徙，未及曩時，而人有所系，吏無苟得，家給人足，即事雖難，轉死溝渠，于時可免。

translations.literal: The terms of prefects and magistrates were fixed at six years; though they might not be transferred in a lifetime, this did not match former times, yet the people had someone to rely on, officials had no easy gains, households were provided for and people had enough—even when affairs were difficult, dying in ditches and canals could at that time be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates served fixed six-year terms; though they might hold office for life without transfer, this fell short of earlier practice, yet the people had officials they could count on, clerks could not profit at will, and households were fed and people provided for—even when times were hard, starving in ditches and canals could then be avoided.

sentences.zh: 凡百戶之鄉，有市之邑，歌謠舞蹈，觸處成群，蓋宋世之極盛也。

translations.literal: In every village of a hundred households, in every market town, songs and dances formed groups wherever one touched—this was the utmost flourishing of the Song age.
translations.idiomatic: In every hamlet of a hundred households and every market town, song and dance gathered wherever one went—such was the Song dynasty at its height.

sentences.zh: 暨元嘉二十七年，舉境外捍，於是傾資掃蓄，猶有未供，深賦厚斂，天下騷動。

translations.literal: When in the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia a campaign was launched to defend the borders, the state poured out its funds and swept clean its stores, yet still could not meet the need; heavy taxes and deep levies set the realm in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, when a border defense campaign was mounted, the state emptied its coffers and stores yet still could not meet demand; oppressive taxes and crushing levies threw the empire into unrest.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄於孝建，兵連不息。

translations.literal: From this time until the Xiaojian era, warfare continued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the Xiaojian reign, war never ceased.

sentences.zh: 以區區江東，蕞爾迫隘，薦之以師旅，因之以凶荒，向時之盛，自此衰矣。

translations.literal: With the mere southeast of the Yangzi, tiny and cramped, further pressed by armies and compounded by famine and disaster, the former flourishing from that time declined.
translations.idiomatic: The small, cramped lands east of the Yangzi, already pressed by armies and then struck by famine and disaster, saw the former prosperity decline from that point on.

sentences.zh: 晉世諸帝多處內房，朝宴所臨，東西二堂而已。

translations.literal: The emperors of the Jin age mostly dwelt in the inner chambers; for court banquets they attended only the Eastern and Western Halls.
translations.idiomatic: Jin emperors mostly lived in the inner quarters; court banquets were held only in the Eastern and Western Halls.

sentences.zh: 孝武末年，清暑方構，及永初受命，無所改作，所居唯稱西殿，不制嘉名，文帝因之，亦有合殿之稱。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu the Clear Summer Pavilion was just being built; when the Yongchu reign began there was no alteration—the residence was simply called the Western Hall, without adopting a fine name; Emperor Wen followed this and also had the name Combined Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's last years the Clear Summer Pavilion was under construction; when the Yongchu reign began nothing was changed—the palace was simply called the Western Hall, without a grand title; Emperor Wen followed suit and also used the name Combined Hall.

sentences.zh: 及孝武承統，制度滋長，犬馬餘菽粟，土木衣綈繡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the throne, institutions grew ever more elaborate: dogs and horses had leftover grain and beans, and timber and earthwork were clothed in silk gauze and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, institutions swelled without limit: dogs and horses had grain to spare, and timber and masonry were draped in silk and brocade.

sentences.zh: 追陋前規，更造正光、玉燭、紫極諸殿。

translations.literal: Following and outdoing the earlier standards, he newly built the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls and others.
translations.idiomatic: Surpassing even earlier models, he built anew the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls and the like.

sentences.zh: 雕欒綺節，珠窗網戶，嬖女幸臣，賜傾府藏，竭四海不供其欲，殫人命未快其心。

translations.literal: Carved beams with brocade ornament, pearl windows and latticed doors, favored women and cherished ministers—gifts emptied the treasury; exhausting the four seas could not supply his desires, and spending all human lives could not satisfy his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Carved beams with brocade tracery, pearl windows and latticed doors, favored women and pet ministers—rewards drained the treasury; the wealth of the four seas could not feed his desires, and the lives of the people could not content his heart.

sentences.zh: 明皇繼祚，彌篤浮侈，恩不恤下，以至橫流。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne, extravagance grew still more intense; his favor did not reach those below, until disorder spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, extravagance deepened further; his grace did not reach the people below, and disorder spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 蒞人之官，遷變歲屬，突不得黔，席未暇暖，蒲、密之化，事未易階。

translations.literal: Officials who came to govern were transferred year by year; their chimneys never turned black, their mats had no time to grow warm—the transformation of Pu and Mi was not easily attained.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who took office were rotated every year; their chimneys never blackened, their mats never warmed—the humane governance of Pu and Mi was not easily achieved.

sentences.zh: 豈徒吏不及古，人乖于昔，蓋由為上所擾，致化莫從。

translations.literal: Was it only that officials did not match antiquity and people diverged from the past? It was because they were disturbed by those above, so that transformation could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: It was not merely that officials fell short of antiquity and the people diverged from former ways; they were harried from above, so that good governance could not take hold.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝承斯奢縱，輔立幼主，思振人瘼，風移百城。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi inherited this luxury and indulgence, assisted in establishing a young ruler, and sought to revive the people's afflictions, shifting customs across a hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi inherited this extravagance, helped place a young emperor on the throne, and sought to relieve the people's suffering, changing customs across the realm.

sentences.zh: 為政未期，擢山陰令傅琰為益州刺史，乃損華反樸，恭己南面，導人以躬，意存勿擾。

translations.literal: Before his term of rule had ended, he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou—then reduced splendor and returned to simplicity, deferring to others while facing south, leading people by his own example, with the intent of non-interference.
translations.idiomatic: Before his reign had run its course, he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou; he then cut back display and returned to simplicity, humbled himself on the throne, led by personal example, and aimed at non-interference.

sentences.zh: 以山陰大邑，獄訟繁滋，建元三年，別置獄丞，與建康為比。

translations.literal: Because Shanyin was a large district and lawsuits proliferated, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison aide was appointed, on a par with Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanyin was a large commandery with heavy litigation, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison aide was appointed, matching the arrangement at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 永明繼運，垂心政術，杖威善斷，猶多漏網，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。

translations.literal: When the Yongming reign succeeded, he devoted attention to the art of governance, wielding authority and judging well, yet many still escaped the net; when chief administrators violated the law, the blade was sealed and execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongming reign he focused on governance, wielding authority with firm judgment, yet many still slipped through; when senior officials broke the law, the sword was drawn and punishment enforced.

sentences.zh: 郡縣居職，以三周為小滿。

translations.literal: Service in commanderies and counties was reckoned in three-year terms as a minor completion.
translations.idiomatic: Terms in commandery and county office were counted in three-year cycles as a minor completion.

sentences.zh: 水旱之災，輒加振恤。

translations.literal: When flood or drought disasters occurred, relief was promptly added.
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought were met with immediate relief.

sentences.zh: 十許年中，百姓無犬吠之驚，都邑之盛，士女昌逸，歌聲舞節，袨服華妝。

translations.literal: For some ten years the common people had no alarm even at a dog's bark; the capital flourished, gentlemen and ladies were at ease, songs and dance flourished, and bright dress and splendid makeup abounded.
translations.idiomatic: For some ten years the people knew no alarm even from a barking dog; the capital thrived, men and women lived at ease, song and dance flourished, and bright dress and fine makeup were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 桃花淥水之間，秋月春風之下，無往非適。

translations.literal: Between peach blossoms and the clear waters of the Lu, beneath autumn moon and spring breeze, nowhere was not pleasant.
translations.idiomatic: Among peach blossoms and the clear Lu waters, under autumn moon and spring breeze, every place was pleasant.

sentences.zh: 明帝自在布衣，達於吏事，及居宸扆，專務刀筆。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming from the time he was in plain cloth understood official affairs; once he occupied the imperial seat, he devoted himself solely to documents and the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had understood official business even as a commoner; once on the throne he devoted himself entirely to paperwork and legal detail.

sentences.zh: 未嘗枉法申恩，守宰由斯而震。

translations.literal: He never bent the law to show favor; prefects and magistrates were thereby awed.
translations.idiomatic: He never bent the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 屬以魏軍入伐，疆埸大擾，兵車連歲，不遑啟居，軍國糜耗，從此衰矣。

translations.literal: Just then Wei armies invaded; the borders were greatly disturbed; war chariots continued year after year without leisure to open the gates and dwell in peace; army and state were wasted, and from this time decline set in.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei armies invaded; the frontiers were thrown into turmoil; war continued year after year without respite; army and state were drained, and decline began from that point.

sentences.zh: 繼以昏亂，政由群孽，賦調雲起，傜役無度。

translations.literal: This was followed by benighted disorder; government passed to a host of villains; taxes and levies rose like clouds, and corvée labor had no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Benighted disorder followed; power fell to a host of villains; taxes and levies rose like clouds, and corvée labor knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 守宰多倚附權門，互長貪虐，裒刻聚斂，侵擾黎甿。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates mostly relied on powerful cliques, each encouraging the other's greed and cruelty, stripping and gathering levies, harassing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates mostly clung to powerful factions, feeding one another's greed and cruelty, extorting and squeezing the people.

sentences.zh: 天下搖動，無所措其手足。

translations.literal: The realm was shaken, and people had nowhere to place their hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was shaken, and the people knew not where to turn.

sentences.zh: 梁武在田，知人疾苦，及定亂之始，仍下寬書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang was still in private station, he knew the sufferings of the people; at the beginning of settling the disorder, he repeatedly issued lenient documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang was still in private station, he knew the people's suffering. At the beginning of settling the disorder, he repeatedly issued lenient orders.

sentences.zh: 東昏時雜調咸悉除省，於是四海之內始得息肩。

translations.literal: The miscellaneous levies from Donghun's time were all abolished and reduced, and thereupon within the four seas people first found rest for their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: The miscellaneous levies from Donghun's time were all abolished or reduced, and only then did people throughout the realm begin to rest their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 及踐皇極，躬覽庶事，日昃聽政，求瘼恤隱。

translations.literal: When he ascended the imperial throne, he personally reviewed the many affairs, heard government business until the sun declined, sought out suffering, and cared for hidden distress.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the imperial throne, he personally reviewed all affairs, heard government business until the sun declined, sought out suffering, and cared for hidden distress.

sentences.zh: 乃命輶軒以省方俗，置肺石以達窮人。

translations.literal: He then ordered light carriages to inspect regional customs and set up the complaint stone so that poor people could reach him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered light carriages to inspect regional customs and set up the complaint stone so that poor people could reach him.

sentences.zh: 勞己所先，事唯急病。

translations.literal: He put his own toil first, and in affairs made urgent suffering his only priority.
translations.idiomatic: He put his own toil first, and in affairs gave priority only to urgent suffering.

sentences.zh: 元年，始去人貲，計丁為布。

translations.literal: In the first year, he first removed the property tax and counted adult males for cloth levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, he abolished the property tax and assessed adult males for cloth levies.

sentences.zh: 在身服浣濯之衣，禦府無文錦之飾。

translations.literal: On his own body he wore washed clothes, and in the imperial storehouses there were no patterned brocade adornments.
translations.idiomatic: He himself wore washed clothes, and the imperial storehouses had no patterned brocade adornments.

sentences.zh: 太官常膳，唯以菜蔬，圓案所陳，不過三盞，蓋以儉先海內也。

translations.literal: The regular meals of the Grand Provisioner used only vegetables; what was set on the round table did not exceed three dishes, for he led the realm first by frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The regular meals of the Grand Provisioner used only vegetables; what was set on the round table did not exceed three dishes. In this way he led the realm first by frugality.

sentences.zh: 故每選長吏，務簡廉平，皆召見於前，親勖政道。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever he selected senior officials, he strove to choose the incorrupt and fair, summoned them all before him, and personally encouraged them in the Way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whenever he selected senior officials, he strove to choose the incorrupt and fair, summoned them before him, and personally encouraged them in governance.

sentences.zh: 始擢尚書殿中郎到溉為建安內史，左戶侍郎劉鬷為晉安太守。

translations.literal: He first promoted Dao Gai, Gentleman of the Palace Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, to be Inner Clerk of Jianan, and Liu Zong, Gentleman of the Left Household Bureau, to be Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He first promoted Dao Gai, Gentleman of the Palace Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, to Inner Clerk of Jianan, and Liu Zong, Gentleman of the Left Household Bureau, to Administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 溉等居官，並以廉潔著。

translations.literal: Gai and the others, while holding office, were all known for incorrupt purity.
translations.idiomatic: Gai and the others, while holding office, were all known for incorrupt purity.

sentences.zh: 又著令：小縣有能，遷為大縣令，大縣有能，遷為二千石。

translations.literal: He also issued an ordinance: if one in a small county had ability, he was promoted to magistrate of a large county; if one in a large county had ability, he was promoted to a two-thousand-dan office.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an ordinance: a capable official in a small county was promoted to magistrate of a large county; a capable official in a large county was promoted to a two-thousand-dan office.

sentences.zh: 於是山陰令丘仲孚有異績，以為長沙內史，武康令何遠清公，以為宣城太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qiu Zhongfu, magistrate of Shanyin, had exceptional achievements and was made Inner Clerk of Changsha; He Yuan, magistrate of Wukang, was pure and fair and was made Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Qiu Zhongfu, magistrate of Shanyin, had exceptional achievements and was made Inner Clerk of Changsha; He Yuan, magistrate of Wukang, was pure and fair and was made Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 剖符為吏者，往往承風焉。

translations.literal: Those who split tallies and served as officials often followed this example.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held official tallies often followed this example.

sentences.zh: 斯亦近代獎勸之方也。

translations.literal: This too was a method of encouragement in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: This too was a method of encouragement in recent times.

sentences.zh: 案前史各立循吏傳，序其德美，今並掇采其事，以備此篇云。

translations.literal: Examining the earlier histories, each established a biography of virtuous officials and set forth their virtuous excellence; now their affairs are gathered and selected together to complete this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories each devoted a chapter to virtuous officials and recounted their excellence; here their deeds are gathered together to fill out this chapter.

sentences.zh: 吉翰字休文，馮翊池陽人也。

translations.literal: Ji Han, style name Xiuwen, was a native of Chiyang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, styled Xiuwen, was a native of Chiyang in Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為龍驤將軍劉道憐參軍，隨府轉征虜左軍參軍，隨道憐北征廣固，賜爵建城縣五等侯。

translations.literal: At first he was aide to Liu Daolian, General Who Inspires Awe; he followed the headquarters and was transferred to Left Army Aide of the General Who Conquers Barbarians, followed Daolian on the northern campaign to Guanggu, and was granted the rank-five marquisate of Jiancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide to Liu Daolian, General Who Inspires Awe; he followed the staff and became Left Army Aide to the General Who Conquers Barbarians, accompanied Daolian on the northern expedition to Guanggu, and was ennobled as a fifth-rank marquis of Jiancheng county.

sentences.zh: 參宋武帝中軍軍事、臨淮太守。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer on military affairs in Emperor Wu of Song's Central Army and as Administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: He served on military staff in Emperor Wu of Song's Central Army and as Administrator of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 復為道憐驃騎中兵參軍，從事中郎。

translations.literal: He again became Central Army Aide to Daolian as Rapid Cavalry General and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He again served Daolian as Central Army Aide under the Rapid Cavalry General and as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 為將佐十餘年，清謹勤正，甚為武帝所知賞。

translations.literal: For more than ten years as a general's aide he was pure, careful, diligent, and upright, and was greatly known and rewarded by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years as a commander's aide he was scrupulous, diligent, and upright, and won high regard from Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，歷位梁、南秦二州刺史，徙益州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia era he successively held the posts of Inspector of Liang and Nanqin, was transferred to Inspector of Yizhou, and received supervisory authority.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he served in turn as Inspector of Liang and Nanqin, was transferred to Inspector of Yizhou, and given supervisory authority.

sentences.zh: 在任著美績，甚得方伯之體，論者稱之。

translations.literal: In office he achieved fine merit, fully possessed the manner of a regional lord, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he achieved distinguished results, fully embodied the role of a regional governor, and won praise from commentators.

sentences.zh: 累遷徐州刺史、監徐兗二州豫州之梁郡諸軍事，時有死罪囚，典簽意欲活之，因翰八關齋呈事，翰省訖，語令且去，明可更呈。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Inspector of Xuzhou and overseer of military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery of Yuzhou; at the time there was a prisoner under sentence of death, and the chief clerk wished to spare him, so during Han's eightfold fast he submitted the matter; Han read it through and told him to withdraw for now and present it again tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Inspector of Xuzhou and supervisor of military affairs in Xu and Yan and Liang commandery of Yuzhou; when a man condemned to death was in custody, the chief clerk wished to save him and submitted the case during Han's eightfold fast; Han read it through and told him to leave and return the next day.

sentences.zh: 明旦，典簽不敢復入，呼之乃來。

translations.literal: The next morning the chief clerk did not dare enter again and came only when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the chief clerk dared not enter until summoned.

sentences.zh: 取昨所呈事視訖，謂曰：「卿意當欲宥此囚死命。

translations.literal: He took yesterday's submission, read it through, and said, "Your intention must be to spare this prisoner's life.
translations.idiomatic: He took up yesterday's submission, read it through, and said, "You mean to spare this prisoner's life.

sentences.zh: 昨於齋坐見其事，亦有心活之。

translations.literal: Yesterday during the fast I saw the matter and also had it in mind to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday during the fast I saw the case and was minded to spare him myself.

sentences.zh: 但此囚罪重，不可全貸，既欲加恩，卿便當代任其罪。」

translations.literal: But this prisoner's crime is grave and cannot be fully pardoned; since you wish to show favor, you should bear his guilt in his place."
translations.idiomatic: But this man's crime is grave and cannot be fully pardoned; since you wish to show mercy, you must bear his guilt in his stead."

sentences.zh: 因命左右收典簽付獄殺之，原此囚生命。

translations.literal: He then ordered attendants to seize the chief clerk, hand him to prison, and execute him, sparing the prisoner's life.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his attendants to seize the chief clerk, send him to prison, and execute him, while sparing the condemned man.

sentences.zh: 其刑政類如此。

translations.literal: His punishments and governance were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His administration of justice was mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 自下畏服，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: Those below feared and submitted; none dared violate his prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Those below feared and obeyed; none dared break his rules.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 杜驥字度世，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ji, style name Dushi, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, styled Dushi, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖預，晉征南將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu was Jin General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu served as Jin General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 曾祖耽，避難河西，因仕張氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi to escape troubles and consequently served the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi during the troubles and entered the service of the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平涼州，父祖始還關中。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Liangzhou, his father and grandfather first returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian pacified Liangzhou, his father and grandfather returned to Guanzhong for the first time.

sentences.zh: 兄坦頗涉史傳，宋武帝平長安，隨從南還。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tan was well versed in historical writings; when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Chang'an, he followed south in the return.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tan was well read in history; when Emperor Wu of Song took Chang'an, he followed the court south.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，位青、冀二州刺史，晚度北人，南朝常以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，每為清途所隔，坦恒以此慨然。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia he held the posts of Inspector of Qing and Ji; as a northerner who had crossed south late, the Southern Court often treated him as crude and rustic; though his talent could have been employed, he was repeatedly blocked from the pure path, and Tan constantly grieved over this.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he served as Inspector of Qing and Ji; as a northerner who had crossed south late, the Southern Court often treated him as a crude outsider; though his talent could have been used, he was repeatedly blocked from high office, and Tan brooded on this constantly.

sentences.zh: 嘗與文帝言及史籍，上曰：「金日磾忠孝淳深，漢朝莫及，恨今世無復此輩人。」

translations.literal: Once when speaking with Emperor Wen about historical records, the emperor said, "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial piety were pure and deep; the Han court could not match him—I regret that in the present age there are no longer men of this kind."
translations.idiomatic: Once when discussing history with Emperor Wen, the emperor said, "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial devotion were profound beyond compare in the Han—how I regret that men like him no longer exist today."

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「日磾之美，誠如聖詔，假使出乎今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Majesty says; but if he appeared in the present age, he would have no leisure beyond tending horses—how could he hope to be recognized?"
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Majesty says—but had he lived in our age, he would have had no time beyond tending horses; how could he have won recognition?"

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也。」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "Why do you measure the court so meanly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "Why do you think so little of the court?"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「請以臣言之，臣本中華高族，亡曾祖因晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Let me speak of myself: I was originally of a lofty clan of the Central States; my deceased great-grandfather, because of the Jin dynasty's disorders, was scattered to the Liang lands—simply because we did not cross south early, we were set apart as crude northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Take my own case: I come from a distinguished Central Plains clan; my late great-grandfather, driven by Jin disorder, fled to the Liang region—simply because we did not cross south early enough, we were dismissed as crude outsiders.

sentences.zh: 日磾胡人，身為牧圉，便超入內侍，齒列名賢。

translations.literal: Midi was a barbarian; though he was a horse-keeper, he was suddenly promoted to inner attendance and ranked among famed worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was a foreigner, a mere groom, yet he was raised straight into the inner service and ranked among the great.

sentences.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。」

translations.literal: Though the sage court may again select talent, I fear it might not be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty's court may promote talent, I fear it would not happen in my case."

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 北土舊法，問疾必遣子弟。

translations.literal: By the old custom of the northern lands, when inquiring after illness one must send one's sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the north it was customary to send one's sons when calling on the sick.

sentences.zh: 驥年十三，父使候同郡韋華。

translations.literal: When Ji was thirteen, his father sent him to call on Wei Hua of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Ji was sent by his father to inquire after Wei Hua of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 華子玄有高名，見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Hua's son Xuan had a lofty reputation; seeing Ji he was struck by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Xuan was highly regarded; struck by the boy, he gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 累遷長沙王義欣後軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Recording Army Aide in the Rear Army of Prince Yixin of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Recording Army Aide in the Rear Army of Prince Yixin of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，隨到彥之入河南，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was given the rank of General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was made General Who Establishes Martiality.

sentences.zh: 魏撤河南戍悉歸河北，彥之使驥守洛陽。

translations.literal: Wei withdrew all garrisons south of the Yellow River to the north of the river; Yanzhi had Ji guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei withdrew its Henan garrisons north of the river, Yanzhi left Ji to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽城廢久，又無糧食，及彥之敗退，驥欲棄城走，慮為文帝誅。

translations.literal: Luoyang had long lain in ruins and had no grain; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wished to abandon the city and flee, fearing execution by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had long been in ruins and had no food; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee, fearing Emperor Wen would execute him.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝平關、洛，致鍾虡舊器南還。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wu pacified Guan and Luo, he had the old bells and tripods brought south.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wu took Guanzhong and Luoyang, he had the ancient bells and vessels brought south.

sentences.zh: 一大鍾墜洛水中，至是帝遣將姚聳夫領千五百人迎致之。

translations.literal: One great bell had fallen into the Luo River; at this time the emperor sent the general Yao Songfu leading fifteen hundred men to receive and bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: One great bell had fallen into the Luo; the emperor now sent General Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.

sentences.zh: 時聳夫政率所領牽鍾于洛水，驥乃遣使紿之曰：「虜既南度，洛城勢弱，今修理城池，並已堅固，軍糧又足，所乏者人耳。

translations.literal: At that time Songfu was just leading his men to haul the bell at the Luo; Ji then sent a messenger to deceive him, saying, "The barbarians have already crossed south; Luoyang is weak in strength—but we are now repairing the walls and they are already firm, and army grain is sufficient; what we lack is only men.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was then hauling the bell at the Luo when Ji sent a messenger to deceive him: "The enemy has crossed south and Luoyang looks weak—but we have repaired the walls and they are strong, and we have ample grain; all we lack is men.

sentences.zh: 君率眾見就，共守此城，大功既立，取鍾無晚。」

translations.literal: If you lead your men to come join us and guard this city together, once the great merit is established, retrieving the bell will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Bring your men and help us hold the city; once that is done, there will be time enough to fetch the bell."

sentences.zh: 聳夫信之，率所領就驥。

translations.literal: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu believed him and marched his men to Ji.

sentences.zh: 及至城不可守，又無糧食，於是引眾去，驥亦委城南奔。

translations.literal: When they arrived the city could not be held and there was no grain; he then led his men away, and Ji also abandoned the city and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived the city could not be held and there was no food; Songfu led his men away, and Ji abandoned the city and fled south.

sentences.zh: 白文帝：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫入城便走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。」

translations.literal: He reported to Emperor Wen: "I originally intended to hold firm unto death, but when Yao Songfu entered the city he fled at once; morale collapsed and could no longer be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Emperor Wen: "I meant to hold to the death, but when Yao Songfu entered the city he fled at once; morale collapsed and could not be restored."

sentences.zh: 上怒，使建威將軍鄭順之殺聳夫于壽陽。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi execute Songfu at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi execute Songfu at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 聳夫，吳興武康人，勇果有氣力，宋偏裨小將莫及。

translations.literal: Songfu was a native of Wukang in Wuxing, brave and resolute with great strength; none of Song's junior generals could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was from Wukang in Wuxing, brave and powerful beyond any of Song's junior officers.

sentences.zh: 十七年，驥為青、冀二州刺史，在任八年，惠化著于齊土。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Ji became Inspector of Qing and Ji; in eight years in office his benevolent governance was renowned in Qi lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Ji became Inspector of Qing and Ji; in eight years his benevolent rule won fame throughout Qi.

sentences.zh: 自義熙至於宋末，刺史唯羊穆之及驥為吏人所稱詠。

translations.literal: From Yixi until the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among inspectors were praised and sung by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: From Yixi to the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among regional governors were praised by officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 後徵為左軍將軍，兄坦代為刺史，北土以為榮焉。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan replaced him as inspector, and northerners regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as General of the Left Army while his brother Tan replaced him as inspector—a source of pride among northerners.

sentences.zh: 坦長子琬為員外散騎侍郎，文帝嘗有函詔敕坦，琬輒開視。

translations.literal: Tan's eldest son Wan was Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Outside the Regular Establishment; Emperor Wen once had a sealed edict for Tan, and Wan opened and read it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's eldest son Wan was an Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; when Emperor Wen sent a sealed edict to Tan, Wan opened and read it.

sentences.zh: 信未及發，又追取之，敕函已發，大相推檢。

translations.literal: The letter had not yet been sent when it was recalled; the sealed edict had already been opened, and a great investigation followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the letter could be sent it was recalled; because the seal had been broken, a major investigation followed.

sentences.zh: 上遣主書詰責驥，並檢開函之主。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a chief clerk to question and blame Ji and also to investigate who had opened the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a chief clerk to rebuke Ji and identify who had broken the seal.

sentences.zh: 驥答曰：「開函是臣第四息季文，伏待刑坐。」

translations.literal: Ji replied, "The one who opened the seal was my fourth son Jiwen; he submits himself to await punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "The one who opened it was my fourth son Jiwen; he submits himself for punishment."

sentences.zh: 上特原不問。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him and did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 第五子幼文薄於行，明帝初，以軍功封邵陽縣男，尋坐巧妄奪爵。

translations.literal: The fifth son Youwen was deficient in conduct; at the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was ennobled as Baron of Shaoyang county for military merit, but soon lost his rank for crafty falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son Youwen was of poor character; early in Emperor Ming's reign he was made Baron of Shaoyang for military merit, but soon lost his title for deceit.

sentences.zh: 後以發太尉廬江王褘謀反事，拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, for exposing the rebellion plot of Grand Marshal Prince Yi of Lujiang, he was appointed Attendant at the Gates and Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for exposing Grand Marshal Prince Yi of Lujiang's plot to rebel, he was appointed Attendant at the Gates and Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽中為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Under the deposed emperor in the Yuanhui era he was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor in the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 幼文所蒞貪橫，家累千金。

translations.literal: In every post he held Youwen was greedy and overbearing, and his household amassed thousands in gold.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held Youwen was greedy and brutal, and his household amassed a fortune in gold.

sentences.zh: 與沈勃、孫超之居止接近，又並與阮佃夫厚善。

translations.literal: He lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi, and was also on close terms with Ruan Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and was close to Ruan Tianfu as well.

sentences.zh: 佃夫既死，廢帝深疾之。

translations.literal: After Tianfu died, the deposed emperor deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianfu's death, the deposed emperor came to hate Youwen deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝微行，夜輒在幼文門墉間聽其弦管，積久轉不能平，於是自率宿衛兵誅幼文、勃、超之等。

translations.literal: The emperor went out incognito and at night would listen to string and pipe music by Youwen's gate; as this continued he could not calm himself, and so he personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out in disguise and at night would listen to music outside Youwen's gate; the resentment built until he led the palace guard himself to kill Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the others.

sentences.zh: 兄叔文為長水校尉，亦誅。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shuwen was Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Water and was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shuwen, Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Water, was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 申恬字公休，魏郡魏人也。

translations.literal: Shen Tian, style name Gongxiu, was a native of Wei in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tian, styled Gongxiu, was a native of Wei in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鍾，為石季龍司徒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong served as Minister of Education under Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhong had been Minister of Education under Shi Jilong.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝平廣固，恬父宣、宣從父兄永皆得歸晉，並以幹用見知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's father's elder cousin Yong both were able to return to Jin and were all known for capability and employment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song took Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's elder cousin Yong were able to return to Jin and won recognition for their ability.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Xuan was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 宣元嘉初，曆兗、青二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia Xuan successively held the posts of Inspector of Yan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia, Xuan served in turn as Inspector of Yan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 恬兄謨與朱修之守滑台。

translations.literal: Tian's elder brother Mo and Zhu Xiuzhi defended Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's elder brother Mo defended Huatai together with Zhu Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 魏克滑台見虜。

translations.literal: Wei captured Huatai and he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Huatai, Mo was captured.

sentences.zh: 後得還，為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return and became Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned and became Administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 恬初為驃騎劉道憐長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Tian at first was senior concurrent acting aide to Liu Daolian, Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Tian first served as senior concurrent acting aide to Liu Daolian, Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 宋受命，辟東宮殿中將軍，度還台，直省十年，不請休急。

translations.literal: When Song received the mandate, he was recruited as Palace General of the Eastern Palace; he crossed back to the capital and served in direct attendance for ten years without requesting leave or urgent rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Song received the mandate, he was appointed Palace General of the Eastern Palace; he returned to the capital and served in direct attendance for ten years without once asking for leave.

sentences.zh: 曆下邳、北海二郡太守，所至皆有政績。

translations.literal: He successively served as Administrator of Xiapi and Beihai; wherever he went he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Xiapi and Beihai in turn, achieving good results everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 又為北譙、梁二郡太守。

translations.literal: He again served as Administrator of Beiqiao and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Beiqiao and Liang.

sentences.zh: 郡境邊接任榛，屢被寇抄。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered on Renzhen and was repeatedly raided by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery bordered Renzhen and was repeatedly raided by bandits.

sentences.zh: 恬到任，密知賊來，乃伏兵要害，出其不意，悉皆禽殄。

translations.literal: When Tian took office he secretly learned the bandits were coming, then ambushed troops at a critical point and, taking them unawares, captured and destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian took office he learned secretly that bandits were coming, set an ambush at a critical point, and surprised and destroyed them all.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，遷督魯東平濟北三郡諸軍事、泰山太守，威惠兼著，吏人便之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to oversee military affairs in the three commanderies of Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and became Administrator of Taishan; authority and kindness were both manifest, and officials and people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was made overseer of military affairs in Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and Administrator of Taishan; his authority and kindness won the loyalty of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，冀州移鎮曆下，以恬為冀州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Ji garrison was moved to Lixia, and Tian was made Inspector of Ji with supervisory authority added.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Ji garrison was moved to Lixia, and Tian was appointed Inspector of Ji with supervisory authority.

sentences.zh: 明年，加濟南太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally made Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also made Administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 孝武踐阼，為青州刺史，尋加督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he became Inspector of Qing, and soon supervisory authority was added.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Tian became Inspector of Qing and soon received supervisory authority.

sentences.zh: 齊地連歲興兵，百姓雕弊，恬防禦邊境，勸課農桑，二三年間，遂皆優實。

translations.literal: Qi lands had raised armies year after year and the people were worn down; Tian defended the borders, encouraged farming and sericulture, and within two or three years all were prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had suffered years of war and the people were exhausted; Tian defended the borders, promoted farming and sericulture, and within two or three years the region was prosperous again.

sentences.zh: 性清約，頻處州郡，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal; though he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts, his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold, and the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature frugal and austere; though he held provincial office repeatedly, his wife and children still knew hunger and cold, and the world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後拜豫州刺史，以疾征還，道卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Yu; summoned back on account of illness, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Inspector of Yu; recalled because of illness, he died on the journey home.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無遺財。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no remaining wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 子寔，南譙太守。

translations.literal: His son Shi was Administrator of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi served as Administrator of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 謨子元嗣，海陵太守。

translations.literal: Mo's son Yuansi was Administrator of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son Yuansi was Administrator of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 元嗣弟謙，臨川內史。

translations.literal: Yuansi's younger brother Qian was Interior Secretary of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi's younger brother Qian was Interior Secretary of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 永子坦，孝建初為太子右衛率，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's son Tan, at the beginning of Xiaojian, became Right Guard Leader of the Crown Prince and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Tan, at the beginning of Xiaojian, became Right Guard Leader of the Crown Prince and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，魏攻兗州，孝武遣太子左衛率薛安都、東陽太守沈法系北捍，至兗州，魏軍已去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, Wei attacked Yanzhou; Emperor Xiaowu sent Xue Andu, Left Guard Leader of the Crown Prince, and Shen Faxi, Administrator of Dongyang, north to defend it. When they reached Yanzhou, the Wei army had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming, Wei attacked Yanzhou. Emperor Xiaowu sent Xue Andu, Left Guard Leader of the Crown Prince, and Shen Faxi, Administrator of Dongyang, north to defend it. When they reached Yanzhou, the Wei army had already gone.

sentences.zh: 坦建議任榛亡命，屢犯邊人，今軍出無功，宜因此翦撲，上從之。

translations.literal: Tan proposed that Ren Zhen's fugitives had repeatedly attacked border people, and now that the army had gone out without achievement, they should take the opportunity to cut them down and strike them; the sovereign followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Tan proposed that Ren Zhen's fugitives had repeatedly attacked border people, and since the army had gone out without achievement, it should take the opportunity to cut them down; the sovereign agreed.

sentences.zh: 亡命先已聞知，舉村逃走，安都、法系坐白衣領職，坦棄市，群臣為請莫得。

translations.literal: The fugitives had already heard of it and the entire village fled. Andu and Faxi were punished by holding office in plain clothes; Tan was sentenced to execution in the marketplace, and though the assembled ministers pleaded for him, they could not obtain pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitives had already heard of it, and the entire village fled. Andu and Faxi were punished by holding office in plain clothes; Tan was sentenced to execution in the marketplace. Though the assembled ministers pleaded for him, they could not obtain pardon.

sentences.zh: 將行刑，始興公沈慶之入市抱坦慟哭曰：「卿無罪，為朝廷所枉誅，我入市亦當不久。」

translations.literal: When the execution was about to be carried out, Duke Shen Qingzhi of Shixing entered the market, embraced Tan, and wailed, saying, "You have no guilt and are being wrongly executed by the court. It will not be long before I too enter the market."
translations.idiomatic: When the execution was about to be carried out, Duke Shen Qingzhi of Shixing entered the market, embraced Tan, and wailed, saying, "You have no guilt and are being wrongly executed by the court. It will not be long before I too enter the market."

sentences.zh: 市官以白上，乃原生命，系尚方。

translations.literal: The market official reported this to the sovereign, who then spared Tan's life and confined him in the imperial workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The market official reported this to the sovereign, who then spared Tan's life and confined him in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 尋被宥，復為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and again became General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pardoned and again became General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子令孫，明帝時為徐州刺史，討薛安都。

translations.literal: His son Lingsun, during Emperor Ming's reign, was Inspector of Xuzhou campaigning against Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsun served as Inspector of Xuzhou under Emperor Ming on a campaign against Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 行至淮陽，即與安都合。

translations.literal: When he reached Huaiyang he immediately joined Andu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.

sentences.zh: 弟闡時為濟陰太守，戍睢陵城，奉順不同安都，安都攻圍不能克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chan was at the time Administrator of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he followed obedience and would not join Andu, and Andu besieged him but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chan was then Administrator of Jiyin, holding Suiling; he remained loyal and refused to join Andu, and Andu besieged the city without success.

sentences.zh: 會令孫至，遣往睢陵說闡，闡降，殺之。

translations.literal: When Lingsun arrived he sent someone to Suiling to persuade Chan; Chan surrendered and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingsun arrived he sent envoys to Suiling to persuade Chan; Chan surrendered and was killed.

sentences.zh: 令孫亦見殺。

translations.literal: Lingsun was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsun was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 杜慧度，交址朱鳶人也。

translations.literal: Du Huidu was a native of Zhuyuan in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu was a native of Zhuyuan in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 本屬京兆。

translations.literal: His clan originally belonged to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was originally registered in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元為甯浦太守，遂居交址。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuan was Administrator of Ningpu and then settled in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuan served as Administrator of Ningpu and settled in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 父瑗字道言，仕州府為日南、九德、交址太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuan, style name Daoyan, served in the provincial administration as Administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan, styled Daoyan, served in the provincial administration as Administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 初，九真太守李遜父子勇壯有權力，威制交土，聞刺史滕遯之當至，分遣二子斷遏水陸津要，瑗收眾斬遜，州境獲寧。

translations.literal: At first Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, and his son were brave and strong with power, dominating Jiaozhi; hearing that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was about to arrive, they sent two sons to block the critical points on land and water; Yuan gathered troops and beheaded Xun, and the province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, and his son were powerful and dominated Jiaozhi; when they heard Inspector Teng Dunzhi was coming, they sent two sons to block the land and water routes; Yuan gathered troops, killed Xun, and restored peace to the province.

sentences.zh: 後為龍驤將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became General Who Inspires Awe and Inspector of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He later became General Who Inspires Awe and Inspector of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝義旗建，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the banner of righteousness, his rank was advanced to General Who Conquers Champions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the banner of righteousness, Yuan was promoted to General Who Conquers Champions.

sentences.zh: 盧循竊據廣州，遣使通好，瑗斬之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun seized Guangzhou and sent envoys seeking alliance; Yuan beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun seized Guangzhou and sent envoys seeking alliance, Yuan had them executed.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年卒，年八十四，贈右將軍。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Yixi at age eighty-four and was posthumously given the title General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Yixi at eighty-four and was posthumously made General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 慧度，瑗第五子也。

translations.literal: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 七年，除交州刺史，詔書未到，其年春，盧循襲破合浦，徑向交州，慧度乃率文武六千人拒循于石碕，破之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhi; before the edict arrived, that spring Lu Xun raided and took Hepu and marched straight on Jiaozhi; Huidu then led six thousand civil and military officials to resist Xun at Shiji and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhi; before the edict arrived, that spring Lu Xun took Hepu and marched on Jiaozhi; Huidu led six thousand officials and soldiers to meet Xun at Shiji and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 循雖破，餘党皆習兵事，李遜子孫李弈、李移、李脫等皆奔竄石碕，盤結俚、獠，各有部曲。

translations.literal: Though Xun was defeated, his remaining followers were all versed in military affairs; Li Xun's descendants Li Yi, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others all fled to Shiji, entrenched among the Li and Liao peoples, each with his own following.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xun was defeated, his followers were seasoned fighters; Li Xun's descendants Li Yi, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others fled to Shiji, entrenched among the Li and Liao tribes, each with his own band.

sentences.zh: 循知弈等與杜氏有怨，遣使招之。

translations.literal: Xun knew that Yi and the others bore a grudge against the Du clan and sent envoys to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun knew Yi and his kin bore a grudge against the Du clan and sent envoys to win them over.

sentences.zh: 弈等受循節度。

translations.literal: Yi and the others accepted Xun's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his followers accepted Xun's command.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，循晨造南津，令三軍入城乃食。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month Xun advanced at dawn on Nanjin and ordered the three armies to enter the city before eating.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month Xun advanced at dawn on Nanjin and ordered his armies not to eat until they had entered the city.

sentences.zh: 慧度悉出宗族私財以充勸賞，自登高艦合戰，放火箭，循眾艦俱然，一時散潰。

translations.literal: Huidu brought out all his clan's private wealth to supply rewards, himself boarded a tall warship to join battle, launched fire arrows, and all of Xun's ships caught fire at once and scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu spent his clan's private wealth on rewards, boarded a tall warship to fight in person, launched fire arrows, and Xun's fleet burst into flame and broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 循中箭赴水死。

translations.literal: Xun was struck by an arrow, entered the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was struck by an arrow, fell into the water, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 斬循及父嘏並循二子，並傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: Xun and his father Gu and Xun's two sons were beheaded, and their heads were sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, his father Gu, and his two sons were beheaded, and their heads were sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 封慧度龍編縣侯。

translations.literal: Huidu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longbian county.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longbian county.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Huidu was promoted to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，南討林邑，林邑乞降，輸生口大象金銀古貝等，乃釋之。

translations.literal: That year he campaigned south against Linyi; Linyi begged to surrender and presented captives, elephants, gold, silver, cowrie shells, and the like, and he then released them.
translations.idiomatic: That year he campaigned south against Linyi; Linyi surrendered and sent captives, elephants, gold, silver, cowrie shells, and the like, and he then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣長史江攸奉表獻捷。

translations.literal: He sent Chief Clerk Jiang You to present a memorial reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chief Clerk Jiang You to present a memorial reporting victory.

sentences.zh: 慧度布衣蔬食，儉約質素。

translations.literal: Huidu wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, being frugal, simple, and unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu wore plain cloth and ate simple food, living frugally and without display.

sentences.zh: 能彈琴，頗好莊、老。

translations.literal: He could play the zither and was rather fond of Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither and was fond of Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祀，崇修學校，歲荒人饑，則以私祿振給。

translations.literal: He prohibited improper sacrifices, promoted and repaired schools, and when years were lean and people hungry, he used his private salary to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He banned improper sacrifices, promoted schools, and when famine struck he used his private salary to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 為政纖密，有如居家，由是威惠沾洽，奸盜不起。

translations.literal: In governing he was meticulous, as if managing a household; thereby authority and kindness permeated, and treachery and theft did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with meticulous care, as if managing his own household; his authority and kindness won the people, and crime ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃至城門不夜閉，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: So much so that city gates were not closed at night and no one picked up lost things on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: City gates were left open at night, and no one picked up lost goods on the roads.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈左將軍。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given the title General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 以慧度長子弘文為振遠將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen was made General Who Quells the Distance and Inspector of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen was appointed General Who Quells the Distance and Inspector of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝北征關、洛，慧度板弘文行九真太守。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Wu campaigned north against Guan and Luo, Huidu appointed Hongwen acting Administrator of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, Huidu appointed Hongwen acting Administrator of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 及繼父為刺史，亦以寬和得眾，襲爵龍編侯。

translations.literal: When he succeeded his father as inspector, he also won the people through leniency and harmony, and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded his father as inspector, he too won the people through leniency and harmony and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，文帝以廷尉王徽為交州刺史，弘文被征，會得重疾，牽以就路。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia Emperor Wen appointed Court Commandant Wang Hui Inspector of Jiaozhi; Hongwen was summoned, and just then fell gravely ill but was dragged onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia Emperor Wen appointed Court Commandant Wang Hui Inspector of Jiaozhi; Hongwen was recalled, fell gravely ill, but was dragged onto the road anyway.

sentences.zh: 親舊見其患篤，勸待病癒。

translations.literal: Kin and friends, seeing how serious his illness was, urged him to wait until he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends, seeing how ill he was, urged him to wait until he recovered.

sentences.zh: 弘文曰：「吾世荷皇恩，杖節三世。

translations.literal: Hongwen said, "Our family for generations has borne the imperial grace and held the staff of office for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen said, "Our family has borne the imperial grace for generations and held office for three generations.

sentences.zh: 常欲投軀帝庭，以報所荷；

translations.literal: I have always wished to offer my body at the imperial court to repay what I have received;
translations.idiomatic: I have always wished to give my life at court to repay what I owe;

sentences.zh: 況親被征命，而可晏然者乎。」

translations.literal: how much more when I am personally summoned—how could I remain at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: how much more when I am personally summoned—how could I remain at ease?"

sentences.zh: 弘文母阮年老，見弘文輿疾就路，不忍別，與到廣州，遂卒。

translations.literal: Hongwen's mother Ruan was old; seeing Hongwen carried sick onto the road, she could not bear to part and accompanied him to Guangzhou, where he then died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Ruan was elderly; unable to bear parting from her sick son as he was carried onto the road, she accompanied him to Guangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 臨死，遣弟弘猷詣建鄴，朝廷甚哀之。

translations.literal: Before death he sent his younger brother Hongyou to Jiankang; the court deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died he sent his younger brother Hongyou to Jiankang; the court mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 孝建中，以豫章太守檀和之為豫州刺史，和之先曆始興太守、交州刺史，所在有威名，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: During Xiaojian, Tan Hezhi, Administrator of Yuzhang, was made Inspector of Yu; Hezhi had previously served as Administrator of Shixing and Inspector of Jiaozhi, and wherever he went had a reputation for authority, and bandits vanished.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaojian, Tan Hezhi, Administrator of Yuzhang, was made Inspector of Yu; he had previously served as Administrator of Shixing and Inspector of Jiaozhi, winning a reputation for authority everywhere he went, and bandits disappeared.

sentences.zh: 每出獵，猛獸伏不敢起。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out hunting, fierce beasts crouched and did not dare rise.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went hunting, fierce beasts crouched and dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 阮長之字景茂，一字善業，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Changzhi, style name Jingmao, also styled Shanye, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Changzhi, styled Jingmao and also Shanye, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖思曠，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sikuan was Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sikuan was Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 父普，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Consulting Army Aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pu was Consulting Army Aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 長之年十五喪父，有孝性，哀感傍人。

translations.literal: Changzhi at fifteen lost his father; he had a filial nature, and his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi lost his father at fifteen; his filial grief moved all who saw him.

sentences.zh: 除服，蔬食者猶積載。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, he still ate only vegetables for years.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he continued to eat only vegetables for years.

sentences.zh: 閒居篤學，未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Living in retirement he studied diligently and never showed a lazy expression.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he studied diligently and never showed a lazy expression.

sentences.zh: 初為諸府參軍，母老，求補襄垣令，督郵無禮鞭之，去職。

translations.literal: At first he was aide in various headquarters; his mother was old, and he sought appointment as Magistrate of Xiangyuan; the postal inspector disrespectfully flogged him, and he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide in various headquarters; when his mother grew old he sought appointment as Magistrate of Xiangyuan; the postal inspector flogged him without cause, and he resigned.

sentences.zh: 後拜武昌太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時王弘為江州，雅相知重，引為車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Hong was in Jiang province and greatly valued him, recommending him as Attendant Gentleman in the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was then in Jiang province and valued him highly, recommending him as Attendant Gentleman in the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年，除臨海太守，在官常擁敗絮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he was appointed Administrator of Linhai; in office he constantly wrapped himself in worn cotton.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he was appointed Administrator of Linhai; in office he constantly wrapped himself in worn cotton padding.

sentences.zh: 至郡少時，母亡，葬畢不勝憂卒。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching the commandery his mother died; when the burial was complete he could not bear his grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after reaching the commandery his mother died; when the burial was over he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 時郡田祿以芒種為斷，此前去官者則一年秩祿皆入後人。

translations.literal: At the time commandery field salaries were reckoned to Mangzhong; before this, when an official left office, a full year's salary all went to his successor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time commandery field salaries were reckoned to Mangzhong; before that, when an official left office, a full year's salary went to his successor.

sentences.zh: 始以元嘉末改此科，計月分祿。

translations.literal: Only at the end of Yuanjia was this rule changed to calculate salary by the month.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of Yuanjia was this changed to monthly calculation of salary.

sentences.zh: 長之去武昌郡，代人未至，以芒種前一日解印綬。

translations.literal: When Changzhi left Wuchang commandery his successor had not yet arrived; he surrendered his seal and cord the day before Mangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhi left Wuchang his successor had not arrived; he surrendered his seal and cord the day before Mangzhong.

sentences.zh: 初發都，親故或以器物贈別，得便緘錄，後歸，悉以還之。

translations.literal: When he first left the capital, kin and friends sometimes gave him objects as parting gifts; he would seal and record them when convenient, and on returning gave them all back.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the capital, kin and friends sometimes gave him parting gifts; he recorded each item and on returning returned them all.

sentences.zh: 為中書郎直省，夜往鄰省，誤著屐出合，依事自列。

translations.literal: As Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat on direct duty, he went at night to the neighboring office, mistakenly wore clogs out of the gate, and reported himself according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat on night duty, he went to a neighboring office, mistakenly wore clogs out of the gate, and reported himself according to regulations.

sentences.zh: 門下以闇夜人不知，不受列。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, on the grounds that it was dark and no one knew, did not accept his report.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, saying that in the dark no one had seen, declined to accept his report.

sentences.zh: 長之固遣送曰：「一生不侮暗室。」

translations.literal: Changzhi firmly sent it in again, saying, "In a lifetime one does not cheat a dark room."
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi insisted on sending it in again: "In a lifetime one does not cheat even a dark room."

sentences.zh: 前後所蒞官，皆有風政，為後人所思。

translations.literal: In every office he held before and after there was exemplary governance, and later people remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held he governed with distinction, and later generations remembered him.

sentences.zh: 宋世言善政者咸稱之。

translations.literal: In the Song age all who spoke of good governance praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song age all who spoke of good governance praised him.

sentences.zh: 文帝深惜之，曰：「景茂方堪大用，豈直以清苦見惜。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply regretted it and said, "Jingmao was just fit for great employment—was he to be valued only for purity and hardship?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen deeply regretted his loss and said, "Jingmao was fit for great employment—was he to be valued only for his austerity?"

sentences.zh: 子師門，原鄉令。

translations.literal: His son Shimen was Magistrate of Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shimen was Magistrate of Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，文帝遣大使巡行四方，兼散騎常侍王歆之等上言：「宣威將軍、陳南頓二郡太守李元德清勤均平，奸盜止息。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia Emperor Wen sent grand envoys to tour the four quarters; Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Wang Xinzhi and others submitted: "General Who Proclaims Prestige and Administrator of the two commanderies Chen and Nandun Li Yuande is pure, diligent, even, and fair; treachery and theft have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia Emperor Wen sent grand envoys to tour the realm; Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Wang Xinzhi and others reported: "General Who Proclaims Prestige and Administrator of Chen and Nandun Li Yuande is pure, diligent, and fair; crime has ceased.

sentences.zh: 彭城內史魏恭子廉惜修慎，在公忘私，安約守儉，久而彌固。

translations.literal: Interior Secretary of Pengcheng Wei Gongzi is frugal, careful, and restrained; in public service he forgets private interest, keeps to simplicity and guards frugality, and over time grows firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Secretary of Pengcheng Wei Gongzi is frugal and careful; in office he forgets private interest, keeps to simplicity, and grows firmer in austerity with time.

sentences.zh: 前宋縣令成浦為政寬濟，遺詠在人。

translations.literal: Former Magistrate of Song county Cheng Pu governed with leniency and relief; his legacy of praise remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Former Magistrate of Song county Cheng Pu governed with leniency and relief; the people still sing his praise.

sentences.zh: 前鮦陽令李熙國在事有方，人思其政。

translations.literal: Former Magistrate of Tiaoyang Li Xiguo in office had method; people remember his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Former Magistrate of Tiaoyang Li Xiguo governed with method; the people still remember his rule.

sentences.zh: 故山桑令何道自少清廉，白首彌厲。

translations.literal: Former Magistrate of Shansang He Dao from youth has been pure and honest; white-haired, he grows ever stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Former Magistrate of Shansang He Dao has been incorruptible since youth and grows ever more rigorous in old age.

sentences.zh: 應加褒賚，以勸於後。」

translations.literal: He ought to receive commendation and bounty, to encourage those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: He should be commended and rewarded as an encouragement to future officials."

sentences.zh: 各被褒賜。

translations.literal: Each was commended and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Each of them was commended and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 歆之字叔道，河東人。

translations.literal: Xinzhi, styled Shudao, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xinzhi, styled Shudao, was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖愆期有名晉世，官至南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qianqi was famous in the Jin age; his office reached Commandant of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qianqi was renowned in the Jin dynasty and rose to Commandant of the Southern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 歆之位左戶尚書、光祿大夫，卒官。

translations.literal: Xinzhi held the posts of Director of the Left Household and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi served as Director of the Left Household and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and died in office.

sentences.zh: 甄法崇，中山人也。

translations.literal: Zhen Fachong was a native of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Fachong was from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 父匡，位少府卿，以清聞。

translations.literal: His father Kuang held the post of Director of Palace Revenues and was known for purity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuang served as Director of Palace Revenues and was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 法崇，宋永初中為江陵令，在任嚴整，縣境肅然。

translations.literal: Fachong in the early Yongchu era of Song served as Magistrate of Jiangling; in office he was strict and orderly, and the county's borders were solemn and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongchu era of Song, Fachong served as Magistrate of Jiangling; his stern, orderly governance left the county tranquil.

sentences.zh: 于時，南平繆士通為江安令卒官，至其年末，法崇在聽事，士通前見。

translations.literal: At that time Miu Shitong of Nanping had died in office as Magistrate of Jiangan; when that year drew to its end, Fachong was in the audience hall when Shitong appeared before him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Miu Shitong of Nanping had died in office as Magistrate of Jiang'an; near year's end, while Fachong sat in his audience hall, Shitong appeared before him.

sentences.zh: 法崇知其已亡，愕然未言。

translations.literal: Fachong knew he was already dead; startled, he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the man was dead, Fachong was stunned and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 坐定，云：「卿縣人宋雅見負米千餘石不還，令兒窮弊不自存，故自訴。」

translations.literal: Once seated, he said: "A man of your county, Song Ya, owes more than a thousand piculs of rice and will not repay; it leaves my son destitute and unable to support himself, so I come to lodge this complaint myself."
translations.idiomatic: When they were seated, Shitong said: "Song Ya of your county owes me more than a thousand piculs of rice and refuses to pay; my son is destitute and cannot survive, so I have come to plead the case myself."

sentences.zh: 法崇因命口受為辭，因遜謝下席。

translations.literal: Fachong thereupon had the complaint taken down by dictation and, with deferential apology, left his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fachong had the complaint transcribed and, with humble apologies, stepped down from his seat.

sentences.zh: 而法崇為問，宋家狼狽輸送。

translations.literal: Then Fachong made inquiry, and the Song family hurriedly delivered payment.
translations.idiomatic: Fachong investigated the matter, and the Song family hastily paid what they owed.

sentences.zh: 太守王華聞而歎美之。

translations.literal: Administrator Wang Hua heard of it and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Hua heard of the affair and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 法崇孫彬。

translations.literal: Fachong's grandson was Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Fachong's grandson was Bin.

sentences.zh: 彬有行業，鄉黨稱善。

translations.literal: Bin had conduct and accomplishment; neighbors and clansmen praised his goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was a man of upright character, and the community spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 嘗以一束苧就州長沙寺庫質錢，後贖苧還，於苧束中得五兩金，以手巾裹之，彬得，送還寺庫。

translations.literal: Once he took a bundle of ramie to the Changsha Temple treasury in the prefecture to pawn for money; later he redeemed the ramie and returned it, and inside the bundle found five taels of gold wrapped in a handkerchief; Bin obtained it and returned it to the temple treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Once he pawned a bundle of ramie at the Changsha Temple treasury for money; when he redeemed and took it back, he found five taels of gold wrapped in a handkerchief inside and returned the gold to the temple.

sentences.zh: 道人驚云：「近有人以此金質錢，時有事不得舉而失。

translations.literal: The monk said in alarm: "Recently someone pawned this gold for money; at the time there was business and it could not be lifted out, and it was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The monk exclaimed in surprise: "Someone recently pawned this gold, but an urgent matter kept us from retrieving it and it was lost.

sentences.zh: 檀越乃能見還，輒以金半仰酬。」

translations.literal: The donor can actually see it returned—let half the gold serve as humble repayment."
