translations.idiomatic: That you would return it is remarkable; please accept half the gold as a reward."

sentences.zh: 往復十餘，彬堅然不受，因謂曰；

translations.literal: Back and forth more than ten times, Bin steadfastly would not accept; then he said to him:
translations.idiomatic: They went back and forth more than ten times, but Bin firmly refused; he then said:

sentences.zh: 「五月披羊裘而負薪，豈拾遺金者邪。」

translations.literal: "In the fifth month one wraps oneself in a sheepskin coat to carry firewood—surely that is not someone who picks up lost gold!"
translations.idiomatic: "Would a man who wears a sheepskin coat in May to gather firewood be one who keeps lost gold?"

sentences.zh: 卒還金。

translations.literal: In the end he returned the gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he returned all the gold.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝布衣而聞之，及踐阼，以西昌侯藻為益州刺史，乃以彬為府錄事參軍，帶郫縣令。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of this while still a commoner in cloth garments; when he ascended the throne, making Marquis of Xichang Zao Prefect of Yizhou, he appointed Bin as Recorder of the Prefectural Headquarters, concurrently Magistrate of Pixian.
translations.idiomatic: While still a commoner, Emperor Wu of Liang heard the story; once enthroned he made Marquis of Xichang Xiao Zao prefect of Yizhou and appointed Bin recorder of his headquarters, with concurrent command of Pixian.

sentences.zh: 將行，同列五人，帝誡以廉慎。

translations.literal: About to depart, five men of the same rank going together—the Emperor admonished them on integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin was about to depart with four colleagues, the Emperor admonished each to govern with integrity and care.

sentences.zh: 至彬，獨曰：「卿昔有還金之美，故不復以此言相屬。」

translations.literal: When it came to Bin, he alone said: "You once had the virtue of returning gold; therefore I need not charge you with these words again."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to Bin, he said alone: "You once returned lost gold; I need not repeat that admonition to you."

sentences.zh: 由此名德益彰。

translations.literal: From this his reputation and virtue grew ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: His fame for virtue spread all the more.

sentences.zh: 及在蜀，藻禮之甚厚云。

translations.literal: When he was in Shu, Zao treated him with great courtesy—it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Xiao Zao treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 傅琰字季珪，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yan, styled Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, styled Jigui, was from Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖弘仁，宋武帝之外弟，以中表曆顯官，位太常卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hongren was a maternal cousin of Emperor Wu of Song; through this kin tie he passed through prominent offices and reached Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hongren was a cousin of Emperor Wu of Song on the maternal side and, through that connection, rose through high office to Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 祖劭字彥先，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao, styled Yanxian, was an External Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu Shao, styled Yanxian, served as External Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父僧佑，山陰令，有能名。

translations.literal: His father Sengyou was Magistrate of Shanyin and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyou was Magistrate of Shanyin and was famed for competence.

sentences.zh: 琰美姿儀，仕宋為武康令，遷山陰令，並著能名，二縣皆謂之傅聖。

translations.literal: Yan was handsome in bearing; serving Song he was Magistrate of Wukang, then transferred to Shanyin; both posts he filled with renown for ability, and both counties called him "Saint Fu."
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and dignified in bearing, Yan served the Song as Magistrate of Wukang and then of Shanyin; in both counties he won fame for ability and both hailed him as "Saint Fu."

sentences.zh: 賜爵新亭侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhui he was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母喪，鄰家失火，延燒琰屋，抱柩不動。

translations.literal: During his mother's mourning, a neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to burn Yan's house; he embraced the coffin and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, a neighbor's fire spread to his house; he clung to the coffin and would not stir.

sentences.zh: 鄰人競來赴救，乃得俱全。

translations.literal: Neighbors rushed one after another to rescue him, and in the end all were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors rushed to help, and mother and coffin were both spared.

sentences.zh: 琰股髀之間已被煙焰。

translations.literal: Between Yan's thighs and shanks he had already been scorched by smoke and flame.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's thighs were already scorched by the flames.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰為山陰令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi was regent, because lawsuits in Shanyin had piled up in vexation, he again made Yan Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent, lawsuits in Shanyin had piled up; he again appointed Yan magistrate there.

sentences.zh: 賣針、賣糖老姥爭團絲來詣琰，琰掛團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。

translations.literal: An old woman who sold needles and an old woman who sold sugar disputed over a ball of silk and came before Yan; Yan hung the silk ball on a pillar and whipped it, secretly observing iron filings—thereupon he punished the sugar-seller.
translations.idiomatic: An old needle-seller and an old sugar-seller quarreled over a ball of silk and came before Yan; he hung the silk on a post and whipped it, spotted iron filings on it, and fined the sugar-seller.

sentences.zh: 又二野父爭雞，琰各問何以食雞，一人云粟，一人云豆。

translations.literal: Again two rustic fellows disputed over a chicken; Yan asked each what he fed the chicken—one said millet, one said beans.
translations.idiomatic: Two farmers disputed ownership of a chicken; Yan asked each what he fed it with—one said millet, the other beans.

sentences.zh: 乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。

translations.literal: He then broke open the chicken and found millet; he convicted the one who had said beans.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered the bird, found millet in its crop, and punished the man who claimed beans.

sentences.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢為偷。

translations.literal: Within the county they called him divine and bright; none dared commit theft.
translations.idiomatic: The county hailed him as uncannily just, and theft ceased.

sentences.zh: 琰父子並著奇績，時雲諸傅有理縣譜，子孫相傳，不以示人。

translations.literal: Yan and his father and son both achieved extraordinary records; at the time it was said the various Fus had a secret manual for governing a county, passed down from generation to generation and not shown to others.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son alike won extraordinary renown; people said the Fu clan kept a secret manual on county governance, handed down among descendants and never shown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 升明中，遷益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era he was transferred to Prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming he was made Prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 自縣遷州，近世罕有。

translations.literal: From county to prefecture—seldom seen in recent generations.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion straight from county magistrate to prefect was rare in recent times.

sentences.zh: 齊建元四年，征驍騎將軍、黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan of Qi he was summoned as General of the Agile Cavalry and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi the fourth year of Jianyuan he was recalled as General of the Agile Cavalry and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 永明中，為廬陵王安西長史、南郡內史，行荊州事。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he served as Chief Administrator to Prince Anxi of Luling, Interior Minister of Nan commandery, and Acting Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming he served as chief administrator to Prince Anxi of Luling, interior minister of Nan commandery, and acting governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 琰喪西還，有詔出臨哭。

translations.literal: When Yan's coffin returned westward, an edict ordered the court to come out and attend the mourning rites with weeping.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan's coffin was borne westward, the throne ordered an imperial mourning visit.

sentences.zh: 時長沙太守王沈、新蔡太守劉聞慰、晉平太守丘仲起、長城縣令何敬叔、故鄣縣令丘寂之，皆有能名，而不及琰也。

translations.literal: At the time Prefect of Changsha Wang Shen, Prefect of Xincai Liu Wenwei, Prefect of Jinping Qiu Zhongqi, Magistrate of Changcheng He Jingshu, and Magistrate of Guzhang Qiu Jizhi all had reputations for ability, yet none matched Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects Wang Shen of Changsha, Liu Wenwei of Xincai, and Qiu Zhongqi of Jinping, and magistrates He Jingshu of Changcheng and Qiu Jizhi of Guzhang all enjoyed reputations for ability—but none equaled Fu Yan.

sentences.zh: 沈字彥流，東海人，曆錢唐、山陰、秣陵令，南平、長沙太守，清廉戒慎，身恒居祿而居處日貧。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Yanliu, was a native of Donghai; he passed through the magistracies of Qiantang, Shanyin, and Moling, and the prefectures of Nanping and Changsha; pure, honest, and cautious, he always held a salary yet his dwelling grew poorer day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, styled Yanliu, of Donghai served as magistrate of Qiantang, Shanyin, and Moling and as prefect of Nanping and Changsha; scrupulously honest and cautious, he lived on his salary yet grew poorer by the day.

sentences.zh: 死之日無宅可憩，故吏為營棺柩。

translations.literal: On the day he died there was no house in which to rest; former subordinates arranged coffin and bier for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he had no home to die in; former staff provided his coffin.

sentences.zh: 聞慰自有傳。

translations.literal: Wenwei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenwei has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 仲起見沈憲傳，敬叔見子思澄傳。

translations.literal: Zhongqi is treated in the biography of Shen Xian; Jingshu in the biography of Zisi Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongqi appears in Shen Xian's biography; He Jingshu in Zisi Cheng's.

sentences.zh: 寂之字德玄，吳興烏程人。

translations.literal: Jizhi, styled Dexuan, was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jizhi, styled Dexuan, was from Wucheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十七，為州西曹，兼直主簿。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he served as Western Section Officer of the prefecture, concurrently acting Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he served as a Western Section officer in the prefecture and acting chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 刺史王彧行縣夜還，前驅已至，而寂之不肯開門，曰：「不奉墨旨。」

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Yu was returning at night from touring the counties; the vanguard had already arrived, yet Jizhi refused to open the gate and said, "I do not have a written order in ink."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Yu was returning at night from a county tour; though the vanguard had arrived, Jizhi refused to open the gate, saying: "I have no written order."

sentences.zh: 彧方于車中為教，然後開。

translations.literal: Yu was just then in his carriage drafting a directive, and only then did he open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu drafted an order in his carriage, and only then did Jizhi admit him.

sentences.zh: 彧歎曰：「不意郅君章近在合下。」

translations.literal: Yu sighed and said: "I did not expect Zhi Junzhang to be right beneath my headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu exclaimed: "I never expected a Zhi Junzhang right under my own roof."

sentences.zh: 即轉為主簿。

translations.literal: He was immediately transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was promptly promoted to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 在縣專以廉潔禦下。

translations.literal: In the county he relied solely on purity and honesty to control subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he governed subordinates through personal integrity alone.

sentences.zh: 于時丹徒縣令沈巑之以清廉抵罪，寂之聞之曰：「清吏真不可為也，政當處季、孟之間乎。」

translations.literal: At that time Magistrate of Dantu Shen Cuanzhi was punished for being pure and honest; hearing it Jizhi said: "A pure official truly cannot be one—ought one not rather stand between Ji and Meng?"
translations.idiomatic: When Magistrate Shen Cuanzhi of Dantu was punished for honesty, Jizhi remarked: "Perhaps an incorruptible magistrate truly cannot survive—maybe one ought to aim somewhere between Ji and Meng after all."

sentences.zh: 巑之吳興武康人，性疏直，在縣自以清廉不事左右，浸潤日至，遂鎖系尚方。

translations.literal: Cuanzhi was a native of Wukang in Wuxing; by nature plain and straight; in the county, considering himself pure and honest, he did not serve those at one's side; slander by drips and drabs came day by day, and in the end he was shackled and imprisoned in the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Cuanzhi, of Wukang in Wuxing, was blunt and upright; believing his honesty sufficient, he courted no patrons; slander accumulated until he was shackled and sent to the Palace Workshops prison.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「一見天子足矣。」

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "One sight of the Son of Heaven is enough."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "One audience with the emperor is enough for me."

sentences.zh: 上召問曰：「復欲何陳？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and asked: "What else do you wish to present?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and asked: "Do you have anything else to say?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「臣坐清所以獲罪。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your subject received punishment because of purity."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I was punished for being honest."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「清復何以獲罪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How does purity again become grounds for punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How does honesty become a crime?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「無以承奉要人。」

translations.literal: He said: "There was no way to wait upon influential men."
translations.idiomatic: Cuanzhi said: "Because I would not fawn on the powerful."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「要人為誰？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Who are the influential men?"
translations.idiomatic: Who are these powerful men?" the emperor asked."

sentences.zh: 巑之以手板四面指曰：「此赤衣諸賢皆是。

translations.literal: Cuanzhi with his rank tablet pointed all around and said: "All these worthy men in red robes are.
translations.idiomatic: Cuanzhi swept his hand tablet around the court: "Every one of these gentlemen in red robes.

sentences.zh: 若臣得更鳴，必令清譽日至。」

translations.literal: If your subject could cry out again, I would surely make the reputation for purity increase day by day."
translations.idiomatic: If I could speak freely again, my reputation for honesty would grow daily."

sentences.zh: 巑之雖危言，上亦不責。

translations.literal: Though Cuanzhi spoke dangerous words, the Emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Though his words were bold, the emperor did not reprove him.

sentences.zh: 後知其無罪，重除丹徒令。

translations.literal: Later knowing he was without guilt, he was again appointed Magistrate of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning he was innocent, the court reappointed him magistrate of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 入縣界，吏人候之，謂曰：「我今重來，當以人肝代米，不然清名不立。」

translations.literal: Entering the county border, officials and people awaited him; he said to them: "I come again now; I shall take human livers in place of rice—otherwise a pure reputation cannot be established."
translations.idiomatic: As he entered the county, officials and commoners came to meet him; he told them: "I return determined to take payment in human flesh instead of grain—otherwise an honest magistrate's name cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 又有汝南周洽，曆句容、曲阿、上虞、吳令，廉約無私，卒于都水使者。

translations.literal: There was also Zhou Qia of Runan, who passed through the magistracies of Jurong, Qu'a, Shangyu, and Wu; frugal and without private interest; he died as Superintendent of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhou Qia of Runan, who served as magistrate of Jurong, Qu'e, Shangyu, and Wu; austere and selfless, he died while serving as superintendent of waterways.

sentences.zh: 無以殯斂，吏人為買棺器。

translations.literal: There was no means for burial and encoffining; officials and people bought coffin and rites for him.
translations.idiomatic: He left nothing for burial; staff and locals bought his coffin.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝聞而非之，曰：「洽累曆名邑而居處不理，遂坐無車宅死，令吏衣棺之，此故宜罪貶，無論褒恤。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi heard and disapproved, saying: "Qia repeatedly passed through famous districts yet kept his dwelling in disorder; he ended sitting without carriage or house when he died, making officials cloth and coffin him—this indeed should be censured and demoted, not to speak of commendation and condolence."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi disapproved: "Qia served famous counties yet lived in squalor; he died without house or carriage and made his staff buy his shroud—such conduct deserves censure, not honors or condolence."

sentences.zh: 乃敕不給贈賻。

translations.literal: An edict was issued refusing funeral gifts and condolence payments.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that no posthumous gifts be granted.

sentences.zh: 琰子翽，為官亦有能名，後為吳令，別建康令孫廉，廉因問曰：「聞丈人發奸擿伏，惠化如神，何以至此？」

translations.literal: Yan's son Hui in office also had a reputation for ability; later as Magistrate of Wu, he was parting from Magistrate of Jiankang Sun Lian; Lian thereupon asked: "I hear your honored father exposed treachery and uncovered the hidden, his gracious transformation like a spirit—how did he reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Hui also won fame in office; when he became magistrate of Wu and was taking leave of Sun Lian, magistrate of Jiankang, Lian asked: "Your father exposed fraud with uncanny insight and governed with almost supernatural effect—how did he achieve it?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「無他也，唯勤而清。

translations.literal: He answered: "There is nothing else—only diligence and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Hui answered: "Nothing mysterious—only diligence and integrity.

sentences.zh: 清則憲綱自行，勤則事無不理。

translations.literal: With purity the laws and net proceed of themselves; with diligence nothing in affairs goes unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity lets the law enforce itself; diligence ensures nothing is left undone.

sentences.zh: 憲綱自行則吏不能欺，事自理則物無疑滯，欲不理得乎。」

translations.literal: When the laws proceed of themselves, clerks cannot deceive; when affairs are settled, things have no doubtful delays—how could one wish for affairs not to be settled?"
translations.idiomatic: When the law runs itself, clerks cannot cheat; when affairs move smoothly, cases do not pile up—how could governance fail?"

sentences.zh: 時臨淮劉玄明亦有吏能，曆山陰、建康令，政常為天下第一，終於司農卿。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had administrative ability; he passed through the magistracies of Shanyin and Jiankang; his governance was often ranked first under Heaven; he ended as Minister of Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai was another gifted administrator; magistrate of Shanyin and Jiankang, his governance was often rated the best in the realm; he ended as minister of grain.

sentences.zh: 後翽又代玄明為山陰令，問玄明曰：「願以舊政告新令尹。」

translations.literal: Later Hui again replaced Xuanming as Magistrate of Shanyin and asked Xuanming: "I wish you would tell the new magistrate of the old administration's methods."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Hui succeeded Xuanming as magistrate of Shanyin, he asked: "Please share your secrets with your successor."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「我有奇術，卿家譜所不載，臨別當相示。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I have a wondrous technique not recorded in your family's genealogy; at parting I shall show you."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming replied: "I have a trick your family manual doesn't record—I'll tell you when we part."

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「作縣令唯日食一升飯而莫飲酒，此第一策也。」

translations.literal: Presently he said: "As magistrate eat only one sheng of rice per day and do not drink wine—this is the first stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said: "As magistrate, eat only a sheng of rice a day and never drink wine—that's the first rule."

sentences.zh: 翽天監中為建康令，復有能名，位驃騎諮議。

translations.literal: Hui in the Tianjian era served as Magistrate of Jiankang; again he had a reputation for ability; his office reached Advisory Censor of the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianjian, Hui served as magistrate of Jiankang with renewed acclaim and rose to advisory censor under the Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子岐。

translations.literal: His son was Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qi.

sentences.zh: 岐字景平，仕梁起家南康王左常侍，後兼尚書金部郎，母憂去職，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Jingping, entered service in Liang as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Nankang; later concurrently Director of the Gold Bureau in the Secretariat; on his mother's mourning he left office and observed mourning to the full in rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, styled Jingping, entered Liang service as attendant to the Prince of Nankang, later serving concurrently as director of the Gold Bureau; he left office to mourn his mother and observed every rite of filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋後疾廢久之，復除始新令。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he was long ill and disabled; he was again appointed Magistrate of Shixin.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was long ill; once recovered he was again appointed magistrate of Shixin.

sentences.zh: 縣人有因鬥相毆而死，死家訴郡，郡錄其仇人，考掠備至，終不引咎。

translations.literal: A man in the county died from a brawl and beating; the dead man's family appealed to the commandery; the commandery arrested his enemy and examined and flogged to the utmost, yet in the end he would not confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: A county man died in a brawl; the victim's family sued at the commandery, which arrested the rival and tortured him thoroughly, but he would not confess.

sentences.zh: 郡乃移獄於縣，岐即令脫械，以和言問之，便即首服。

translations.literal: The commandery then transferred the case to the county; Qi immediately had the shackles removed and questioned him with gentle words, and at once he confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery transferred the case to the county; Qi had the man unshackled, questioned him gently, and he confessed at once.

sentences.zh: 法當償死，會冬節至，岐乃放其還家。

translations.literal: By law he should repay with death; it happened that the winter festival arrived, and Qi thereupon released him to return home.
translations.idiomatic: By law he was liable to death; when the winter festival came, Qi released him to go home.

sentences.zh: 獄曹掾固爭曰：「古者有此，今不可行。」

translations.literal: The Prison Section Assistant firmly remonstrated: "Antiquity had this practice; today it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: The prison clerk objected strongly: "Ancient times allowed this, but not today."

sentences.zh: 岐曰：「其若負信，縣令當坐。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "If he betrays trust, the magistrate should bear punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "If he breaks his word, I alone should answer for it."

sentences.zh: 竟如期而反。

translations.literal: In the end he returned on schedule as promised.
translations.idiomatic: The man returned on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 太守深相歎異，遽以狀聞。

translations.literal: The Administrator deeply sighed in wonder and immediately reported the circumstances upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was deeply impressed and reported the matter at once.

sentences.zh: 岐後去縣，人無老少皆出境拜送，號哭聞數十里。

translations.literal: Later when Qi left the county, people regardless of old or young all went beyond the border to bow and send him off; wailing and crying were heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi later left the county, young and old alike went beyond the border to bid him farewell; their lamentations could be heard for miles.

sentences.zh: 至都，除廷尉正，入兼中書通事舍人，累遷安西中記室，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital he was appointed Director of Correct Judgments in the Court of Judicial Review; entering service he concurrently served as Palace Message Bearer of the Secretariat Chancery; through successive promotions he reached Middle Recorder of the Army of the West, concurrently holding the message-bearer post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he was made director of corrections in the court of judicial review and concurrently palace message bearer; he rose to middle recorder on the staff of the Army of the West while retaining his concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 岐美容止，博涉能占對。

translations.literal: Qi had beautiful appearance and bearing; he was broadly learned and able in responses.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was handsome and well composed, widely read, and quick with a reply.

sentences.zh: 大同中與魏和親，其使歲中再至，常遣岐接對焉。

translations.literal: In the Datong era Liang made peace through marriage with Wei; their envoys arrived twice within the year, and Qi was regularly sent to receive and respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong, Liang entered a marriage alliance with Wei; envoys came twice a year, and Qi was regularly assigned to receive them.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，累遷太僕，司農卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, Qi was repeatedly promoted to Minister Coachman and Chamberlain for the National Treasury, while remaining palace message bearer as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing, Qi was repeatedly promoted to Minister Coachman and Chamberlain for the National Treasury, while remaining palace message bearer as before.

sentences.zh: 岐在禁省十餘年，機事密勿，亞于朱異。

translations.literal: Qi spent more than ten years in the palace offices; in confidential affairs of state, he was second only to Zhu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi spent more than ten years in the palace offices; in confidential affairs of state, he was second only to Zhu Yi.

sentences.zh: 此年冬，貞陽侯蕭明伐彭城，兵敗，囚于魏。

translations.literal: That winter, Xiao Ming, Marquis of Zhenyang, campaigned against Pengcheng, his army was defeated, and he was imprisoned by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Xiao Ming, Marquis of Zhenyang, campaigned against Pengcheng, was defeated, and was imprisoned by Wei.

sentences.zh: 二年，明遣使還述魏欲通和好，敕有司及近臣定議。

translations.literal: In the second year, Ming sent an envoy back to state that Wei wished to open friendly relations, and an edict ordered the responsible offices and close ministers to settle the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Ming sent an envoy back to state that Wei wished to open friendly relations, and an edict ordered the responsible offices and close ministers to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 左衛朱異曰：「邊境且得靜寇息人，於事為便。」

translations.literal: Zhu Yi of the Left Guard said, "For the border temporarily to quiet raiders and give the people rest would be convenient for affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi of the Left Guard said, "For the border temporarily to quiet raiders and give the people rest would be convenient."

sentences.zh: 議者並然之。

translations.literal: The deliberators all agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberators all agreed.

sentences.zh: 岐獨曰：「高澄既新得志，何事須和？

translations.literal: Qi alone said, "Gao Cheng has just achieved his ambition; why would he need peace?
translations.idiomatic: Qi alone said, "Gao Cheng has just achieved his ambition; why would he need peace?

sentences.zh: 必是設間，故令貞陽遣使，令侯景自疑，當以貞陽易景，景意不安，必圖禍亂。

translations.literal: This must be a scheme of estrangement: they deliberately had Zhenyang send an envoy to make Hou Jing suspicious of himself. They will exchange Zhenyang for Jing; Jing's mind will become unsettled, and he will certainly plot disaster and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: This must be a scheme of estrangement: they deliberately had Zhenyang send an envoy to make Hou Jing suspicious. They will exchange Zhenyang for Jing; Jing will become uneasy and will certainly plot disaster.

sentences.zh: 若許通好，政是墮其計中。

translations.literal: If we permit friendly relations, this is precisely falling into their plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we permit friendly relations, we are falling straight into their plan.

sentences.zh: 且彭城去歲喪師，渦陽復新敗退，今使就和，益示國家之弱。

translations.literal: Moreover, at Pengcheng last year we lost an army, and at Woyang we have again newly been defeated and retreated. If we now send an envoy to make peace, it will further show the weakness of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at Pengcheng last year we lost an army, and at Woyang we have again just been defeated and driven back. If we now send an envoy to make peace, it will further display the state's weakness.

sentences.zh: 和不可許。」

translations.literal: Peace cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Peace cannot be permitted."

sentences.zh: 異等固執，帝遂從之。

translations.literal: Yi and the others firmly persisted, and the emperor finally followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others firmly persisted, and the emperor finally followed them.

sentences.zh: 及遣使，景果有此疑，遂舉兵入寇，請誅朱異。

translations.literal: When the envoy was sent, Jing indeed had this suspicion, then raised troops and invaded, requesting that Zhu Yi be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy was sent, Jing indeed grew suspicious, then raised troops and invaded, demanding that Zhu Yi be executed.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷中領軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Central Army Commander; his message-bearer post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to central army commander while retaining his concurrent post as palace message bearer.

sentences.zh: 二月，侯景于闕前通表，乞割江右四州安置部下，當解圍還鎮。

translations.literal: In the second month Hou Jing presented a memorial at the palace gate, begging to cede the four provinces south of the Yangtze to settle his followers and promising to lift the siege and return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Hou Jing submitted a memorial before the palace gates, asking to surrender four provinces south of the Yangtze to resettle his troops and pledging to lift the siege and withdraw to his post.

sentences.zh: 敕許之，乃於城西立盟。

translations.literal: An imperial edict granted it, and they thereupon established an alliance west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and an alliance was sworn west of the city.

sentences.zh: 求遣召宣城王出送。

translations.literal: He requested that the Prince of Xuancheng be summoned out to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing demanded that the Prince of Xuancheng be sent out to see him off.

sentences.zh: 岐固執宣城王嫡嗣之重，不宜許之。

translations.literal: Qi firmly held that the weight of the Prince of Xuancheng as legitimate heir was too great and that it should not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi insisted that the Prince of Xuancheng, as the legitimate heir, must not be sent.

sentences.zh: 乃遣石城公大款送之。

translations.literal: They thereupon sent the Prince of Shicheng, Dakuan, to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: They sent the Prince of Shicheng, Dakuan, in his stead.

sentences.zh: 及與景盟訖，城中文武喜躍，冀得解圍。

translations.literal: When the alliance with Jing was concluded, civil and military officials within the city rejoiced and leaped, hoping to obtain relief from the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Once the treaty with Hou Jing was signed, officials and soldiers in the city exulted, hoping the siege would end.

sentences.zh: 岐獨言於眾曰：「賊舉兵為逆，豈有求和。」

translations.literal: Qi alone said to the crowd: "The rebel raised troops in treason—how could he seek peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi alone told the assembly: "This outlaw took up arms in rebellion—how can he truly want peace?"

sentences.zh: 及景背盟，莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: When Jing broke the alliance, none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing broke the treaty, everyone marveled at Qi's foresight.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔，以岐勤勞，封南豐縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict: because of Qi's diligent service, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon followed enfeoffing him as Marquis of Nanfeng for his loyal service.

sentences.zh: 固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 宮城失守，岐帶疾出圍，卒於宅。

translations.literal: When the palace city fell, Qi, though ill, broke out of the encirclement and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace city fell, Qi broke out of the siege despite illness and died at his home.

sentences.zh: 虞願字士恭，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan, styled Shigong, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan, styled Shigong, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖賚，給事中、監利侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji was a Supervising Attendant and Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji held the posts of supervising attendant and Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 父望之早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wangzhi died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wangzhi died early.

sentences.zh: 賚中庭橘樹冬熟，子孫競來取之。

translations.literal: In Ji's courtyard an orange tree ripened in winter; descendants competed to come and pick from it.
translations.idiomatic: An orange tree in Ji's courtyard bore fruit in winter, and the grandchildren scrambled to pick it.

sentences.zh: 願年數歲獨不取，賚及家人皆異之。

translations.literal: Yuan at several years of age alone did not take any; Ji and the family all considered him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was only a few years old, he alone refused to take any; Ji and the whole family found it remarkable.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，為湘東王國常侍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song he served as Regular Attendant in the princely establishment of the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanjia of Liu Song he was a regular attendant in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 及明帝立，以願儒吏學涉，兼蕃國舊恩，意遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, because Yuan combined Confucian learning with administrative skill and also had old favor from the princely state, his treatment was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, he treated Yuan with exceptional favor, valuing both his learning and his service in the former prince's household.

sentences.zh: 除太常丞，尚書祠部郎，通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant in the Ministry of Ceremonies, Director in the Ancestral Temple Bureau of the Secretariat, and Unembellished Cavalier Attendant of the Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant in the Ministry of Ceremonies, director in the ancestral temple bureau, and unembellished cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝性猜忌，體肥憎風，夏月常著小皮衣。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was suspicious; corpulent in body, he hated wind, and in summer months often wore a small fur jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suspicious by nature, corpulent and averse to drafts; even in summer he often wore a light fur vest.

sentences.zh: 拜左右二人為司風令史，風起方面，輒先啟聞。

translations.literal: He appointed two attendants as Wind-Monitoring Clerks; whenever wind arose from any quarter they first reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed two attendants as wind clerks to report the moment a breeze rose from any direction.

sentences.zh: 星文災變，不信太史，不聽外奏，敕靈台知星二人給願，常內省直，有異先啟，以相檢察。

translations.literal: As for astral signs and calamitous changes, he did not trust the Grand Astrologer and would not listen to outside reports; he ordered two star-knowers of the Observatory to serve Yuan, always on duty within the palace; if anything was unusual they reported first, to supervise and inspect each other.
translations.idiomatic: Distrusting the court astronomer, he would hear no outside reports of omens; instead he assigned two observatory astrologers to Yu Yuan, stationed permanently inside the palace to watch the skies and report anomalies to each other.

sentences.zh: 帝以故宅起湘宮寺，費極奢侈。

translations.literal: The emperor raised the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence; the expense was extremely extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: On the site of his old residence the emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple at extravagant cost.

sentences.zh: 以孝武莊嚴刹七層，帝欲起十層，不可立，分為兩刹，各五層。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan pagoda had seven tiers; the emperor wished to build ten tiers, but it could not stand; it was divided into two pagodas, each of five tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Pagoda had seven stories; the emperor wanted ten, but that proved impossible, so he built two five-story pagodas instead.

sentences.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡還見帝，曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi, Administrator of Xin'an, on returning after leaving his commandery came to see the emperor and said: "Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple?
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office as prefect of Xin'an, Chao Shangzhi visited the emperor and asked: "Have Your Majesty seen the Xiang Palace Temple yet?

sentences.zh: 我起此寺是大功德。」

translations.literal: My raising of this temple is great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Building this temple is a great act of merit."

sentences.zh: 願在側曰：「陛下起此寺，皆是百姓賣兒貼婦錢，佛若有知，當悲哭哀湣。

translations.literal: Yuan, at his side, said: "Your Majesty's raising of this temple—all of it is money from common people selling their sons and pawning their wives; if the Buddha had knowledge, he would weep in sorrow and pity.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan, standing beside him, said: "Every coin that built this temple came from common folk who sold their sons and pawned their wives. If the Buddha knew, he would weep in pity.

sentences.zh: 罪高佛圖，有何功德！」

translations.literal: Sin towers over the Buddha-image—what merit is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Your sin outstrips any stupa—where is the merit in that!"

sentences.zh: 尚書令袁粲在坐，為之失色。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yuan Can was present and lost color on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Can, who was present, turned pale.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，使人驅曳下殿，願徐去無異容。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly raged and had men drag him down from the hall; Yuan departed slowly without change of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him dragged from the hall; Yuan withdrew unhurriedly, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩，少日中已復召入。

translations.literal: Because of old favor, within less than half a day he was summoned back in.
translations.idiomatic: Out of lingering affection, the emperor recalled him before half a day had passed.

sentences.zh: 帝好圍碁，甚拙，去格七八道，物議共欺為第三品，與第一品王抗圍碁，依品賭戲。

translations.literal: The emperor loved weiqi but was very clumsy, deviating seven or eight points from correct play; public opinion collectively deceived him into the third rank; he played weiqi against Wang Kang of the first rank and gambled by rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved weiqi but played poorly, often misplacing stones by seven or eight intersections; court gossip humored him with a third-class ranking, and he wagered by rank against first-class player Wang Kang.

sentences.zh: 抗饒借帝，曰：「皇帝飛碁，臣抗不能斷。」

translations.literal: Kang indulgently yielded to the emperor and said: "Your Majesty's flying stones—subject Kang cannot cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang deliberately lost and said: "Your Majesty's stones fly so swiftly that I cannot block them.'

sentences.zh: 帝終不覺，以為信然，好之愈篤。

translations.literal: The emperor to the end did not perceive it, believed it true, and loved it all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never caught on, took it as truth, and grew all the fonder of the game.

sentences.zh: 願又曰：「堯以此教丹朱，非人主所宜好也。」

translations.literal: Yuan again said: "Yao used this to teach Dan Zhu—it is not what a ruler should favor."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan said again: "Yao taught Dan Zhu with this game—it is no pastime fit for a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 雖數忤旨，而蒙賞賜猶異餘人。

translations.literal: Though he repeatedly went against the emperor's wishes, the rewards he received were still unlike those of others.
translations.idiomatic: Though he often contradicted the throne, he continued to receive favors beyond those granted to others.

sentences.zh: 遷兼中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrently serve as Gentleman of the Secretariat Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，愿常侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay ill in bed, Yuan constantly attended with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell bedridden, Yu Yuan attended him constantly with medicines.

sentences.zh: 帝尤好逐夷，以銀缽盛蜜漬之，一食數缽。

translations.literal: The emperor especially loved zhuyi; in silver bowls he stored them steeped in honey, eating several bowls at one sitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was especially fond of cured fish zhuyi, kept in silver bowls steeped in honey; he could eat several bowls at a sitting.

sentences.zh: 謂揚州刺史王景文曰：「此是奇味，卿頗足不？」

translations.literal: He said to Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Yang Province: "This is a rare flavor—do you have enough of it?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yangzhou inspector Wang Jingwen: "This is a rare delicacy—do you have much of it?"

sentences.zh: 景文答曰：「臣夙好此物，貧素致之甚難。」

translations.literal: Jingwen answered: "Your subject has long loved this delicacy; in poverty and plain living it is very hard to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen answered: "I have always loved it, but in my poor, simple life it is hard to come by."

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 食逐夷積多，胸腹痞脹，氣將絕。

translations.literal: Eating zhuyi accumulated in great quantity; chest and belly became distended and blocked; his breath was nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: After consuming too much zhuyi, his chest and belly swelled with distension until he could hardly breathe.

sentences.zh: 左右啟飲數升酢酒，乃消。

translations.literal: Attendants reported that drinking several sheng of vinegar wine would dissolve it.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants advised several pints of vinegar wine, and the swelling subsided.

sentences.zh: 疾大困，一食汁滓猶至三升。

translations.literal: The illness grew severely afflicted; at one meal the dregs and juices still reached three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, he still consumed three sheng of the fish liquor and dregs at a single sitting.

sentences.zh: 水患積久，藥不復效。

translations.literal: Water-illness accumulated over long time; medicine no longer had effect.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic edema set in, and medicines ceased to work.

sentences.zh: 大漸日，正坐呼道人，合掌便絕。

translations.literal: On the day of his great decline he sat upright, summoned a Daoist master, joined palms, and at once expired.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he sat upright, summoned a Daoist priest, joined his palms in prayer, and died.

sentences.zh: 願以侍疾久，轉正員郎。

translations.literal: Because Yuan had long attended the illness, he was made a full regular gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: For his long service at the emperor's sickbed, Yu Yuan was promoted to a regular secretary post.

sentences.zh: 出為晉平太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Jinping.

sentences.zh: 在郡不事生業。

translations.literal: In the commandery he did not pursue livelihood enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he took no part in profit-seeking enterprise.

sentences.zh: 前政與百姓交關，質錄其兒婦，願遣人於道奪取將還。

translations.literal: The previous administration had dealings with common people and held their daughters-in-law as security; Yuan sent men on the road to seize them back and return them.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had taken commoners' daughters-in-law as hostages for debts; Yu Yuan sent men to intercept them on the road and restore them to their families.

sentences.zh: 在郡立學堂教授。

translations.literal: In the commandery he established a school hall for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a school in the prefecture and taught there himself.

sentences.zh: 郡舊出髯蛇，膽可為藥。

translations.literal: The commandery had long produced bearded snakes; their gall could serve as medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The region was known for bearded snakes, whose gall was prized for medicine.

sentences.zh: 有遺願蛇者，願不忍殺，放二十里外山中。

translations.literal: When someone presented Yuan with a snake, he could not bear to kill it and released it in the mountains twenty li away.
translations.idiomatic: When someone brought him a snake, he would not kill it and had it released twenty li into the hills.

sentences.zh: 一夜蛇還床下。

translations.literal: In one night the snake returned beneath the bed.
translations.idiomatic: One night the snake came back and lay beneath his bed.

sentences.zh: 復送四十里山，經宿復歸。

translations.literal: He again sent it forty li into the mountains; after one night it returned once more.
translations.idiomatic: He had it taken forty li into the mountains, but overnight it returned again.

sentences.zh: 論者以為仁心所致。

translations.literal: Discussants held that this was caused by his humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: Observers attributed it to the power of his compassion.

sentences.zh: 海邊有越王石，常隱雲霧，相傳云：「清廉太守乃得見」。

translations.literal: By the seashore there was a stone called the Yue King's Stone, usually hidden in clouds and mist; tradition said, "Only a pure and upright administrator can see it."
translations.idiomatic: A stone called the Yue King's Stone stood by the sea, usually veiled in mist; legend held, "Only an upright prefect can see it clearly."

sentences.zh: 願往就觀視，清澈無所隱蔽。

translations.literal: Yuan went to approach and observe it; it was clear without anything hidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yuan went to look, the stone stood plain and unobscured.

sentences.zh: 後琅邪王秀之為郡，與朝士書曰：「此郡承虞公之後，善政猶存，遺風易遵，差得無事。」

translations.literal: Later when the Prince of Langye, Xiuzhi, was in the commandery, he wrote to court gentlemen: "This commandery follows after Lord Yu; good governance still remains, the lingering influence is easy to follow, and things are tolerably without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Xiuzhi of Langye governed the prefecture, he wrote to colleagues at court: "This commandery still bears Lord Yu's legacy; his good order endures and his example is easy to follow, so affairs here are largely untroubled."

sentences.zh: 以母老解職，除後軍將軍。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he resigned office and was appointed General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to care for his aged mother and was appointed general of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回嘗詣願，願不在，見其眠床上積塵埃，有書數帙。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui once called on Yuan; Yuan was not in; he saw dust accumulated on the sleeping bed and several bundles of books.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui once called on Yu Yuan and found him out; dust lay thick on the bed, with only a few bundles of books.

sentences.zh: 彥回歎曰：「虞君之清至於此。」

translations.literal: Yanhui sighed and said: "Lord Yu's purity reaches to this point."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui sighed: "Lord Yu's austerity runs this deep.'

sentences.zh: 令人掃地拂床而去。

translations.literal: He had someone sweep the floor and dust the bed, then left.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the room swept and the bed dusted, then departed.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat Chancery and concurrently served as Libationer of the Eastern Hall Archives.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary and appointed libationer of the Eastern Pavilion archives.

sentences.zh: 兄季為上虞令卒，願從省步出還家，不待詔便歸東。

translations.literal: His older brother Ji died while Magistrate of Shangyu; Yuan left the provincial office on foot to return home and, without waiting for an edict, returned east at once.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Ji died in office as magistrate of Shangyu, Yu Yuan walked out of the capital and went home without waiting for leave.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，遷廷尉，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Valiant Cavalry; transferred to Minister of Justice; his libationer post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the valiant cavalry, then minister of justice, while retaining his archive post.

sentences.zh: 願嘗事宋明帝，齊初，神主遷汝陰廟，願拜辭流涕。

translations.literal: Yuan had once served Emperor Ming of Song. At the beginning of Qi, when the spirit tablet was moved to the Ruyin temple, Yuan bowed in farewell and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan had once served Emperor Ming of Song. At the beginning of Qi, when the spirit tablet was transferred to the Ruyin temple, Yuan bowed farewell to it with tears streaming down.

sentences.zh: 建元元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 願著五經論問，撰會稽記，文翰數十篇。

translations.literal: Yuan wrote Questions and Discussions on the Five Classics, compiled the Record of Kuaiji, and produced several dozen pieces of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan wrote Questions and Discussions on the Five Classics, compiled the Record of Kuaiji, and left several dozen literary works.

sentences.zh: 王洪范，上穀人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hongfan was a man of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongfan was from Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，魏克青州，洪範得別駕清河崔祖歡女，仍以為妻。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Song, when Wei captured Qing Province, Hongfan obtained the daughter of Assistant Administrator Cui Zuhuan of Qinghe and took her as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi of Liu Song, when Northern Wei seized Qing Province, Hongfan married the daughter of Cui Zuhuan, an assistant administrator from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖歡女說洪范南歸。

translations.literal: Cui Zuhuan's daughter persuaded Hongfan to return south.
translations.idiomatic: His wife persuaded him to flee south.

sentences.zh: 宋桂陽王之難，隨齊高帝鎮新亭，常以身捍矢。

translations.literal: In the crisis of the Prince of Guiyang of Song, he followed Emperor Gao of Qi in holding Xinting and often used his body to shield against arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the rebellion of the Prince of Guiyang, he followed Xiao Daocheng at Xinting and repeatedly shielded him with his own body.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「我自有楯，卿可自防。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said: "I have my own shield—you should protect yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said: "I have my own shield—you should look to your own safety."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「天下無洪范何有哉，蒼生方亂，豈可一日無公。」

translations.literal: He answered: "If there were no Hongfan under Heaven, what would remain? The common people are in disorder—how could there be one day without Your Grace?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "What would become of the realm without Wang Hongfan? The people are in turmoil—how can you be spared for even a day?"

sentences.zh: 帝甚賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly prized him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 後為晉壽太守，多昧贓賄，為州所按。

translations.literal: Later as Administrator of Jinshou he concealed many bribes and presents and was investigated by the province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as prefect of Jinshou, he took numerous bribes and was investigated by the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 大懼，棄郡奔建鄴。

translations.literal: Greatly afraid, he abandoned the commandery and fled to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, he abandoned his post and fled to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 高帝輔政，引為腹心。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao served as regent, he drew him in as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Daocheng held regency, he drew Hongfan into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為青、冀二州刺史，悔為晉壽時貨賕所敗，更勵清節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was Inspector of Qing and Ji Provinces; repenting that at Jinshou he had been ruined by bribes and gifts, he again urged himself toward pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwu he became inspector of Qing and Ji; ashamed of his corruption at Jinshou, he resolved to govern with integrity.

sentences.zh: 先是青州資魚鹽之貨，或強借百姓麥地以種紅花，多與部下交易，以祈利益。

translations.literal: Previously Qing Province relied on goods of fish and salt; some forcibly borrowed common people's wheat fields to plant safflower, and often traded with subordinates to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Province had long profited from fish and salt; officials forced farmers to lend wheat fields for safflower, traded with subordinates, and skimmed profits at every turn.

sentences.zh: 洪軌至，一皆斷之。

translations.literal: When Honggui arrived, he cut off all of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Honggui took office, he put a stop to all such practices.

sentences.zh: 啟求侵魏，得黃郭、鹽倉等數戍。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting raids on Wei and obtained several garrison posts including Huangguo and the Salt Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to strike into Wei territory and captured several outposts, including Huangguo and Yancang.

sentences.zh: 後遇敗，死傷塗地，深自咎責。

translations.literal: Later he met defeat; the dead and wounded covered the ground; he deeply blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he suffered a crushing defeat with terrible casualties and blamed himself bitterly.

sentences.zh: 乃于謝祿山南除地，廣設茵席，殺三牲，招戰亡者魂祭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon south of Mt. Xielu he cleared ground, broadly spread cushioned mats, slaughtered the three sacrificial beasts, and summoned the souls of those killed in battle to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the south slope of Mt. Xielu he cleared a field, spread mats, sacrificed the three beasts, and summoned the souls of the fallen.

sentences.zh: 人人呼名，躬自沃酹，仍慟哭不自勝，因發病而亡。

translations.literal: Calling each man by name, he personally poured libations; still he wailed beyond control; thereupon illness arose and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He called out each man's name, poured libations himself, and wept until he collapsed; the grief brought on illness, and he died.

sentences.zh: 洪範既北人而有清正，州人呼為「虜父使君」，言之咸落淚。

translations.literal: Hongfan, though a northerner, had purity and integrity; people of the province called him "Barbarian Father Governor"; when they spoke of him all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Though a northerner, Hongfan had won a reputation for integrity; locals called him "the barbarian father prefect," and mention of his name brought tears.

sentences.zh: 永明中，有江夏李珪之字孔璋，位尚書右丞，兼都水使者，曆職稱為清能。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era there was Li Guizhi of Jiangxia, styled Kongzhang; he held the post of Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Commissioner of Waterways; through successive offices he was called pure in ability.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, Li Guizhi of Jiangxia, styled Kongzhang, served as right assistant director of the Secretariat and commissioner of waterways; in every post he was praised for clean competence.

sentences.zh: 後兼少府卒。

translations.literal: Later while concurrently serving as Minister of the Palace Treasury he died.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while also serving as minister of the palace treasury.

sentences.zh: 沈瑀字伯瑜，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yu, style name Boyu, was from Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu, style name Boyu, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父昶，事宋建平王景素。

translations.literal: His father Chang served Jingsu, Prince of Jianping under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang served Jingsu, Prince of Jianping under Song.

sentences.zh: 景素謀反，昶先去之，及敗坐繫獄。

translations.literal: When Jingsu plotted rebellion, Chang had left him beforehand, but when Jingsu was defeated Chang was implicated and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu plotted rebellion, Chang had left him beforehand, but when Jingsu was defeated Chang was implicated and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 瑀詣台陳請得免罪，由是知名。

translations.literal: Yu went to the court offices and presented a plea, obtaining exemption from guilt; because of this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went to the court offices and presented a plea, obtaining exemption from guilt; because of this he became known.

sentences.zh: 為奉朝請，嘗詣齊尚書左丞殷濔，濔與語及政事，甚器之，謂曰：「觀卿才幹，當居吾此職。」

translations.literal: He became a Court Gentleman for Consultation and once visited Yin Mi, Left Assistant in the Qi Department of State Affairs. Mi spoke with him about government affairs, thought highly of him, and said, "Observing your talent and ability, you ought to occupy this office of mine."
translations.idiomatic: He became a Court Gentleman for Consultation and once visited Yin Mi, Left Assistant in the Qi Department of State Affairs. Mi spoke with him about government affairs, thought highly of him, and said, "Judging from your talent and ability, you ought to hold this office of mine."

sentences.zh: 司徒竟陵王子良聞瑀名，引為府行參軍，領揚州部傳從事。

translations.literal: Ziliang, Prince of Jingling and Minister of Education, heard Yu's name and brought him in as acting aide in his office, concurrently serving as courier aide for the Yangzhou section.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang, Prince of Jingling and Minister of Education, heard Yu's name and brought him in as acting aide in his office, concurrently serving as courier aide for the Yangzhou section.

sentences.zh: 時建康令沈徽孚恃勢傲瑀，瑀以法繩之，眾憚其強。

translations.literal: At that time Shen Huifu, magistrate of Jiankang, relied on his power and was arrogant toward Yu; Yu restrained him by law, and everyone feared his firmness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shen Huifu, magistrate of Jiankang, relied on his power and treated Yu arrogantly. Yu restrained him by law, and everyone feared his firmness.

sentences.zh: 子良甚相知賞，雖家事皆以委瑀。

translations.literal: Ziliang understood and appreciated him greatly, and even entrusted family affairs to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang understood and appreciated him greatly, and even entrusted family affairs to Yu.

sentences.zh: 子良薨，瑀復事刺史始安王遙光，嘗使送人丁，速而無怨，遙光謂同使吏曰：「爾何不學沈瑀所為。」

translations.literal: When Ziliang died, Yu again served Yaoguang, Prince of Shian and provincial inspector. Once, when sent to deliver conscripted men, he was swift and caused no resentment; Yaoguang told the officials sent with him, "Why do you not learn from what Shen Yu does?"
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang died, Yu again served Yaoguang, Prince of Shian and provincial inspector. Once, when sent to deliver conscripted men, he was swift and caused no resentment; Yaoguang told the officials sent with him, "Why do you not learn from what Shen Yu does?"

sentences.zh: 乃令瑀專知州獄事。

translations.literal: He then ordered Yu to take sole charge of the province's prison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Yu to take sole charge of the province's prison affairs.

sentences.zh: 湖熟縣方山埭高峻，冬月，公私行侶以為艱。

translations.literal: At Hushu County the Fangshan dam was high and steep; in winter months public and private travelers found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At Hushu the Fangshan embankment was steep and treacherous in winter for all who passed.

sentences.zh: 明帝使瑀行修之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Yu to go and repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming dispatched Shen Yu to repair it.

sentences.zh: 瑀乃開四洪，斷行客就作，三日便辦。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon opened four flood channels; he cut off passing travelers to put them to work; in three days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu opened four sluice channels and pressed travelers into labor; the work was done in three days.

sentences.zh: 揚州書佐私行，詐稱州使，不肯就作，瑀鞭之四十。

translations.literal: A Yang Province clerical assistant traveled privately, falsely claimed to be a provincial envoy, and refused to work; Yu whipped him forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: A Yangzhou clerk traveling privately claimed to be on provincial business and refused to work; Shen Yu had him flogged forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 書佐歸訴遙光，遙光曰：「沈瑀必不枉鞭汝。」

translations.literal: The clerk returned and complained to Yaoguang; Yaoguang said: "Shen Yu would certainly not whip you without cause."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk complained to Xiao Yaoguang, who said: "Shen Yu would never flog you unjustly."

sentences.zh: 覆之果有詐。

translations.literal: On reviewing the matter it proved there had indeed been fraud.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation confirmed the deception.

sentences.zh: 明帝復使瑀築赤山塘，所費減材官所量數十萬。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming again had Yu build the Chishan dike; the expenditure was reduced by several hundred thousand from what the Materiel Bureau estimated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again put Shen Yu in charge of the Chishan dike, and the cost fell hundreds of thousands below the materiel bureau's estimate.

sentences.zh: 帝益善之。

translations.literal: The emperor all the more favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought still more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 為建德令，教人一丁種十五株桑、四株柿及梨栗，女子丁半之。

translations.literal: As Magistrate of Jiande he ordered each adult male to plant fifteen mulberry trees, four persimmon trees, and pear and chestnut trees; for adult females half as much.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jiande he required each adult male to plant fifteen mulberries, four persimmons, and pears and chestnuts; women planted half as many.

sentences.zh: 人咸歡悅，頃之成林。

translations.literal: People all rejoiced; in no time it became forest.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed the policy gladly, and before long the land was forested.

sentences.zh: 去官還都，兼行選曹郎，隨陳伯之軍至江州。

translations.literal: Leaving office, Yu returned to the capital, concurrently acted as Gentleman of the Selection Bureau, and followed Chen Bozhi's army to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office, Yu returned to the capital, concurrently acted as Gentleman of the Selection Bureau, and followed Chen Bozhi's army to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會梁武起兵圍郢城，瑀說伯之迎武帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops and besieged Yingcheng, Yu persuaded Bozhi to welcome Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops and besieged Yingcheng, Yu persuaded Bozhi to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 伯之泣曰：「餘子在都。」

translations.literal: Bozhi wept and said, "My remaining children are in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi wept and said, "My remaining children are in the capital."

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「不然人情匈匈，皆思改計；若不早圖，眾散難合」。

translations.literal: Yu said, "No. People's feelings are in turmoil, and all are thinking of changing plans; if you do not plan early, once the crowd disperses it will be hard to gather them."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "No. People's feelings are in turmoil, and everyone is thinking of changing plans; if you do not plan early, once the crowd disperses it will be hard to gather them."

sentences.zh: 伯之遂降。

translations.literal: Bozhi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，瑀在竟陵王家，素與範雲善，齊末嘗就雲宿，夢坐屋梁柱上，仰見天中有字曰：「范氏宅」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu was in the household of the Prince of Jingling, he had long been friendly with Fan Yun. At the end of Qi he once lodged with Yun and dreamed he was sitting on a roof beam and pillar; looking up, he saw characters in the sky saying, "Fan clan residence."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yu was in the household of the Prince of Jingling, he had long been friendly with Fan Yun. At the end of Qi he once lodged with Yun and dreamed he was sitting on a roof beam; looking up, he saw characters in the sky saying, "Fan clan residence."

sentences.zh: 至是瑀為帝說之，帝曰：「雲得不死，此夢可驗。」

translations.literal: At this point Yu told the emperor about it, and the emperor said, "If Yun can avoid death, this dream may be verified."
translations.idiomatic: At this point Yu told the emperor about it, and the emperor said, "If Yun can avoid death, this dream may be verified."

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，雲深薦瑀，自暨陽令擢兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yun strongly recommended Yu, and from magistrate of Jiyang he was promoted to concurrently serve as Right Assistant in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Yun strongly recommended Yu, and from magistrate of Jiyang he was promoted to concurrently serve as Right Assistant in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時天下初定，陳伯之言瑀催督運輸，軍國獲濟。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had just been settled, and Chen Bozhi said that Yu had hastened and supervised transport, enabling army and state to be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm had just been settled, and Chen Bozhi said that Yu had hastened and supervised transport, enabling army and state to be supplied.

sentences.zh: 帝以為能，遷尚書駕部郎，兼右丞如故。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable and promoted him to Gentleman of the Carriage Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, while he remained concurrent Right Assistant as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered him capable and promoted him to Gentleman of the Carriage Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, while he remained concurrent Right Assistant as before.

sentences.zh: 瑀薦族人沈僧隆、僧照有吏幹，帝並納之。

translations.literal: Yu recommended his clansmen Shen Senglong and Sengzhao as having administrative ability, and the emperor accepted both recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu recommended his clansmen Shen Senglong and Sengzhao as having administrative ability, and the emperor accepted both recommendations.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，起為余姚令。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother, then was recalled to serve as Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother, but was later appointed magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 縣大姓虞氏千餘家，請謁如市，前後令長莫能絕。

translations.literal: In the county the great clan Yu had more than a thousand households; requests for audience were like a market; magistrates before and after could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand households of the great Yu clan lived in the county, and their petitions for favors swarmed like a marketplace—no previous magistrate had been able to put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 自瑀到，非訟訴無所通，以法繩之。

translations.literal: From the time Yu arrived, except for lawsuits nothing was admitted; he bound them with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shen Yu took office, no petition would be heard unless it was a legal dispute, and he enforced the law against them.

sentences.zh: 縣南又有豪族數百家，子弟縱橫，遞相庇蔭，厚自封植，百姓甚患之。

translations.literal: South of the county there were again several hundred powerful clans; their sons and younger men ran rampant, shielding one another in turn, enriching themselves heavily, and the common people greatly suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the county lived several hundred powerful clans whose sons swaggered unchecked, shielding one another and entrenching their privileges—the people of the district suffered greatly under them.

sentences.zh: 瑀召其老者為石頭倉監，少者補縣僮，皆號泣道路，自是權右屏跡。

translations.literal: Yu summoned their elders to serve as overseers of the Shitou granary and their younger men to fill county laborer posts; all wailed and wept on the roads; from then on the powerful held back and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu assigned their elders as overseers of the Shitou granary and their young men as county laborers; the clans wept openly in the streets, and from then on the local power-brokers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 瑀初至，富吏皆鮮衣美服以自彰別，瑀怒曰：「汝等下縣吏，何得自擬貴人！」

translations.literal: When Yu first arrived, wealthy clerks all wore bright clothes and fine garments to set themselves apart; Yu angrily said: "You are low county clerks—how dare you compare yourselves to noblemen!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yu first arrived, the better-off clerks all dressed in fine silks to distinguish themselves. He thundered: "You are county clerks—how dare you comport yourselves like grandees!"

sentences.zh: 悉使著芒屨粗布，侍立終日，足有蹉跌，輒加榜捶。

translations.literal: He had them all wear straw sandals and coarse cloth, standing in attendance all day; if their feet stumbled he immediately added beating with the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: He made them all wear straw sandals and coarse cloth and stand attendance all day; the moment one of them stumbled, he had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 瑀微時嘗至此鬻瓦器，為富人所辱，故因以報焉。

translations.literal: In his humble youth Yu had once come here to sell pottery and was insulted by a rich man; therefore he now took revenge thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Shen Yu had sold pottery here and been humiliated by a wealthy man—this was how he settled the score.

sentences.zh: 由是士庶駭怨。

translations.literal: From this gentry and commoners were shocked and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and commoners were both shocked and resentful.

sentences.zh: 瑀廉潔自守，故得遂行其意。

translations.literal: Yu was upright and clean in self-restraint, and therefore was able to carry out his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shen Yu was incorruptible and held himself strictly to account, he was able to enforce his will.

sentences.zh: 後為安南長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Administrator of Annan and Prefect of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed chief administrator of Annan and prefect of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史曹景宗卒，仍為信威蕭穎達長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Jiang Province Cao Jingzong died, he continued as Chief Administrator to Xinyi Xiao Yingda while his post as prefect remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Jingzong, inspector of Jiang Province, died, Shen Yu became chief administrator to General Xinyi Xiao Yingda while retaining his post as prefect.

sentences.zh: 瑀性屈強，每忤穎達，穎達銜之。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was stubborn; he repeatedly offended Yingda, and Yingda bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu was obstinate by nature and frequently crossed Xiao Yingda, who took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 天監八年，因入諮事，辭又激厲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian, when he entered to consult on affairs, his words were again forceful and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianjian, when he came in to discuss official business, his language was once again fierce and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 穎達作色曰：「朝廷用君作行事邪？」

translations.literal: Yingda changed color and said: "Did the court appoint you to serve as a clerk?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingda flushed with anger and said: "Did the court appoint you to be a mere clerk?"

sentences.zh: 瑀出，謂人曰：「我死而後已，終不能傾側面從。」

translations.literal: Yu went out and said to people: "I shall not stop until I die; I can never bow and turn my face to follow."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu left and said to those around him: "I shall not stop until I am dead—I will never bow my head and defer to him."

sentences.zh: 是日于路為人所殺，多以為穎達害焉。

translations.literal: That same day on the road he was killed by someone; many believed Yingda had done it.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was murdered on the road; most people believed Xiao Yingda was responsible.

sentences.zh: 子續累訟之。

translations.literal: His son Xu repeatedly brought lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen Xu brought lawsuit after lawsuit over the murder.

sentences.zh: 遇穎達尋卒，事不窮竟。

translations.literal: When Yingda soon after died, the matter was not pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingda died shortly afterward, and the case was never fully resolved.

sentences.zh: 續乃布衣蔬食終其身。

translations.literal: Xu thereupon wore plain cloth and ate vegetables for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xu spent the rest of his life in plain cloth and simple fare, living as a mourner.

sentences.zh: 范述曾字子玄，一字穎彥，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shuzeng, courtesy name Zixuan, also styled Yingyan, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng, whose courtesy name was Zixuan and who was also known as Yingyan, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，從餘杭呂道惠受五經，略通章句。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; he studied the Five Classics under Lu Daohui of Yuhang and had a general grasp of commentary and phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning from childhood and studied the Five Classics under Lu Daohui of Yuhang, gaining a working knowledge of textual commentary.

sentences.zh: 道惠曰：「此子必為王者師。」

translations.literal: Daohui said: "This boy will surely become a teacher to kings."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daohui said of him: "This boy will one day teach princes."

sentences.zh: 齊文惠太子、竟陵文宣王幼時，齊高帝引述曾為之師友，起家宋晉熙王國侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince of Wenhu and Prince of Wenxuan of Jingling were young, Emperor Gao of Qi brought in Shuzeng as their teacher and friend; he first entered service as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Prince of Jinxi of Song.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Crown Prince Wenhui and Prince Wenxuan of Jingling were still children, Emperor Gao of Qi brought Fan Shuzeng in as their tutor and companion; he first entered office as a gentleman of Prince Jinxi's kingdom under Song.

sentences.zh: 齊初至南郡王國郎中令，遷太子步兵校尉，帶開陽令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he reached Director of the Kingdom of the Prince of Nankang, was transferred to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Foot Soldiers, and concurrently served as Magistrate of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi he rose to director of the Prince of Nankang's household, then became colonel of the crown prince's foot soldiers while also serving as magistrate of Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 述曾為人騫諤，在宮多所諫爭，太子雖不能全用，然亦弗之罪也。

translations.literal: Shuzeng as a man was blunt and outspoken; in the palace he often remonstrated and disputed; although the crown prince could not fully employ his advice, he nevertheless did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng was blunt and outspoken; in court he remonstrated frequently. The crown prince could not always heed him, yet never held it against him.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王深相器重，號為周舍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling deeply valued and esteemed him and called him Zhou She.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling held him in the highest regard and nicknamed him Zhou She.

sentences.zh: 太子左衛率沈約亦以述曾方汲黯。

translations.literal: The Left Guard Leader of the Crown Prince Shen Yue also likened Shuzeng to Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, leader of the crown prince's left guard, compared Fan Shuzeng to the Han minister Ji An.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝即位，為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi ascended the throne, Shuzeng became Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi ascended the throne, Shuzeng became Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 為政清平，不尚威猛，甿俗便之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and fair and did not esteem harsh severity, and the common customs found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was pure and fair and did not value harsh severity, and the common people found it agreeable.

sentences.zh: 所部橫陽縣山谷嶮峻，為逋逃所聚，前後二千石討捕莫能息。

translations.literal: In Hengyang County under his jurisdiction, the mountains and valleys were steep and rugged, and fugitives gathered there; previous two-thousand-dan officials had tried to suppress and arrest them but none could stop them.
translations.idiomatic: In Hengyang County under his jurisdiction, the mountains and valleys were steep and rugged, and fugitives gathered there. Previous two-thousand-dan officials had tried to suppress and arrest them, but none could stop them.

sentences.zh: 述曾下車，開示恩信，凡諸凶黨，繈負而出，編戶屬籍者二百餘家。

translations.literal: As soon as Shuzeng arrived, he opened and showed kindness and trust; all the violent bands came out carrying infants on their backs, and more than two hundred households were registered and attached to the household rolls.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Shuzeng arrived, he displayed kindness and trust; all the violent bands came out carrying infants on their backs, and more than two hundred households were registered on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 自是商旅流通，居人安業。

translations.literal: From then on merchants and travelers moved freely, and residents were at peace in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: From then on merchants and travelers moved freely, and residents were secure in their work.

sentences.zh: 勵志清白，不受饋遺。

translations.literal: He set his will on purity and integrity and accepted no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He set his will on purity and integrity and accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 明帝下詔褒美，徵為遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued an edict praising him and summoned him as General of Mobile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming issued an edict praising him and summoned him as General of Mobile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 郡送故舊錢二十餘萬，一無所受，唯得白桐木火籠樸十餘枚而已。

translations.literal: The commandery sent more than two hundred thousand cash from old acquaintances, but he accepted none of it, receiving only a little over ten plain white paulownia braziers.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery sent more than two hundred thousand cash from old acquaintances, but he accepted none of it, receiving only a little over ten plain white paulownia braziers.

sentences.zh: 東昏時，拜中散大夫，還鄉里。

translations.literal: Under Donghun, he was appointed Grandee of Palace Leisure and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Under Donghun, he was appointed Grandee of Palace Leisure and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝踐阼，乃輕行詣闕，仍辭還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, he traveled lightly to the palace gate, then declined office and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, Fan Shuzeng traveled lightly to the capital to pay his respects, then declined office and went home.

sentences.zh: 武帝下詔褒美，以為太中大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict praising and commending him and appointed him Grand Master of Palace Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict praising him and appointed him grand master of palace eminence.

sentences.zh: 述曾生平所得奉祿，皆以分施，及老遂壁立無資。

translations.literal: All the salary Shuzeng received in his lifetime he distributed in gifts; when old he was left with nothing standing like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng gave away every salary he ever received; in old age he was left with nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 以天監八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 注易文言，著雜詩賦數十篇。

translations.literal: He annotated the Wenyan section of the Changes and composed several dozen miscellaneous poems and rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a commentary on the Wenyan section of the Book of Changes and composed several dozen poems and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 後有吳興丘師施亦廉潔稱，罷臨安縣還，唯有二十籠簿書，並是倉庫券帖。

translations.literal: Later there was Qiu Shishi of Wuxing, also famed for integrity and cleanliness; when he left office as Magistrate of Lin'an and returned, he had only twenty baskets of ledgers, all warehouse vouchers and receipts.
