translations.idiomatic: Later there was Qiu Shishi of Wuxing, likewise renowned for integrity; when he left his post as magistrate of Lin'an, he carried home only twenty baskets of records—all warehouse vouchers and receipts.

sentences.zh: 當時以比述曾。

translations.literal: At the time people compared him to Shuzeng.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time compared him to Fan Shuzeng.

sentences.zh: 位至台郎。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of clerk on the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孫謙字長遜，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Sun Qian, courtesy name Changxun, was a man of Ju in Dongguan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, courtesy name Changxun, was a native of Ju in Dongguan commandery.

sentences.zh: 客居曆陽，躬耕以養弟妹，鄉里稱其敦睦。

translations.literal: He lived as a guest in Liyang, personally farming to support his younger brother and sisters; the village praised his warmth and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He lived as a guest in Liyang, farming with his own hands to support his younger siblings; neighbors praised his devotion to family.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為句容令，清慎強記，縣人號為神明。

translations.literal: He served Song as Magistrate of Jurong, clear and cautious with a strong memory; the county people called him divine spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he served as magistrate of Jurong, where his integrity, caution, and remarkable memory earned him the nickname "the divine magistrate."

sentences.zh: 宋明帝以為巴東、建平二郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song appointed him Prefect of the two commanderies of Badong and Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song appointed him governor of the Badong and Jianping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 郡居三峽，恒以威力鎮之。

translations.literal: The commanderies lay in the Three Gorges and were always held in check by force of power.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies lay in the Three Gorges and had always been held by force of arms.

sentences.zh: 謙將述職，敕募千人自隨。

translations.literal: When Qian was about to report to his duties, an edict ordered recruiting a thousand men to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Qian was about to take up his post, the court ordered him to recruit a thousand men as an escort.

sentences.zh: 謙曰：「蠻夷不賓，蓋待之失節耳。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The barbarians do not submit—it is simply because they are treated without proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian said: "The tribal peoples are unruly only because they have not been treated with proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 何煩兵役，以為國費。」

translations.literal: Why trouble military service and make it a state expense?"
translations.idiomatic: Why burden the state with military expenses?"

sentences.zh: 固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 至郡，布恩惠之化，蠻獠懷之，競餉金寶。

translations.literal: When he reached the commandery he spread a transforming policy of grace and favor; the tribal peoples cherished him and competed to offer gold and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Once at his post he spread benevolent governance; the tribal peoples came to trust him and competed to offer gold and treasure.

sentences.zh: 謙慰喻而遣，一無所納。

translations.literal: Qian comforted and instructed them and sent them away; he accepted not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian gently declined and sent them away, accepting nothing.

sentences.zh: 及掠得生口，皆放還家。

translations.literal: When captives were taken in raids he released them all to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners were captured in raids, he released them all to return home.

sentences.zh: 奉秩出吏人者，悉原除之。

translations.literal: All minor officials whose salaries fell short he fully remitted and cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted all debts owed by minor officials from their salaries.

sentences.zh: 郡境翕然，威恩大著。

translations.literal: Within the commandery all was harmonious; his authority and grace were greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery grew peaceful, and his authority and kindness became widely known.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，征還為撫軍中兵參軍，遷越騎校尉、征北司馬。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was recalled and made Middle Army Aide to the Pacification General, then transferred to Colonel of Swift Cavalry and Northern Campaign Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was recalled to serve as middle army aide to the commander-in-chief, then promoted to colonel of swift cavalry and northern campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 府主建平王將稱兵，患謙強直，托事遣使至都，然後作亂。

translations.literal: The lord of the headquarters, the Prince of Jianping, was about to raise troops; fearing Qian's firm uprightness, he sent him on a mission to the capital under a pretext, then afterward launched rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jianping, his commanding lord, planned to rebel; fearing Sun Qian's upright character, he sent him on a mission to the capital on a pretext, then launched his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及建平誅，遷左軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Jianping was executed he was transferred to General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince was executed, Sun Qian was transferred to general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 齊初，為錢唐令，禦煩以簡，獄無系囚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he served as Magistrate of Qiantang, handling troubles with simplicity; the prison had no detained prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi he served as magistrate of Qiantang, cutting through complexity with simplicity so that no prisoners remained in the jail.

sentences.zh: 及去官，百姓以謙在職不受餉遺，追載縑帛以送之。

translations.literal: When he left office the common people, because Qian during his tenure had not accepted gifts, pursued him with carts loaded with silk to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office the people pursued him with carts of silk, for he had accepted no gifts during his tenure.

sentences.zh: 謙辭不受。

translations.literal: Qian declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian refused them.

sentences.zh: 每去官輒無私宅，借空車廄居焉。

translations.literal: Each time he left office he had no private residence and borrowed empty stables to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he left office he had no home of his own and lived in rented empty stables.

sentences.zh: 永明初，為江夏太守，坐被代輒去郡，系尚方，頃之，免為中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he served as Prefect of Jiangxia; he was charged with leaving the commandery as soon as he was replaced, was imprisoned at the Palace Workshop, and shortly after was released and made Palace Attendant Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongming era he served as governor of Jiangxia but was dismissed immediately upon being replaced, imprisoned at the palace workshop, and though soon released was appointed palace attendant grandee.

sentences.zh: 明帝將廢立，欲引謙為心膂，使兼衛尉，給甲仗百人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was about to depose and establish an heir he wished to draw Qian as trusted inner support, made him concurrently Commandant of the Guard, and granted a hundred armored guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming planned to depose the heir he wanted Sun Qian as a trusted advisor, made him concurrent commandant of the guard, and granted him a hundred armored guards.

sentences.zh: 謙不願處際會，輒散甲士，帝雖不罪而弗復任焉。

translations.literal: Qian was unwilling to stand at a critical juncture and immediately dispersed the armored soldiers; although the emperor did not punish him, he never again employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, unwilling to be caught up in such intrigues, immediately dispersed the soldiers; though the emperor did not punish him, he never employed him again.

sentences.zh: 梁天監六年，為零陵太守，年已衰老，猶強力為政，吏人安之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian of Liang he served as Prefect of Lingling; though already aged and frail he still vigorously administered affairs, and officials and people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian under Liang he became governor of Lingling; though advanced in years he still administered vigorously, bringing ease to officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 先是郡多猛獸暴，謙至絕跡。

translations.literal: Before this the commandery had many fierce beasts causing havoc; when Qian arrived they vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Before his arrival the commandery had been plagued by fierce beasts; once Sun Qian took office they vanished entirely.

sentences.zh: 及去官之夜，猛獸即害居人。

translations.literal: On the night he left office the fierce beasts immediately harmed the residents.
translations.idiomatic: On the very night he left office, the beasts returned and attacked the people.

sentences.zh: 謙為郡縣，常勤勸課農桑，務盡地利，收入常多於鄰境。

translations.literal: When Qian served in commanderies and counties he always diligently urged agricultural and sericultural work, striving to exhaust the land's advantage; revenues were always greater than in neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his service as magistrate and governor he diligently promoted agriculture and silk production, fully exploiting the land's potential so that revenues consistently exceeded those of neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 九年，以老徵為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned on account of age to serve as Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled due to age and appointed minister of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 及至，帝嘉其清潔，甚禮異焉。

translations.literal: When he arrived the emperor praised his clarity and cleanliness and treated him with exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at court the emperor commended his integrity and treated him with special honor.

sentences.zh: 每朝見，猶請劇職自效。

translations.literal: At every court audience he still requested strenuous duties to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: At every court audience he still asked for demanding posts where he could serve.

sentences.zh: 帝笑之曰：「朕當使卿智，不使卿力。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "I shall employ your wisdom, not your strength."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said: "I shall use your wisdom, not your strength."

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔加優秩，給親信二十人，並給扶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict added enhanced rank, granted twenty personal attendants, and also provided walking supports.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict granted him enhanced rank, twenty personal attendants, and walking supports.

sentences.zh: 謙自少及老，曆二縣五郡，所在廉潔。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Qian passed through two counties and five commanderies; everywhere he was upright and clean.
translations.idiomatic: From youth through old age, across two counties and five commanderies, Sun Qian remained incorruptible wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 居身儉素，床施蘧蒢屏風。

translations.literal: In his personal conduct he was frugal and plain; his bed had rush matting and a reed screen.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply—a bed with rush matting and a reed screen.

sentences.zh: 冬則布被莞席。

translations.literal: In winter he used a cloth quilt and cattail mat.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he slept under a cloth quilt on a cattail mat.

sentences.zh: 夏日無幬帳，而夜臥未嘗有蚊蚋，人多異焉。

translations.literal: In summer he had no curtains or canopies, yet when he slept at night he never had mosquitoes or gnats; many people found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Even in summer he used no curtains or mosquito netting, yet he was never bitten at night—a thing many found remarkable.

sentences.zh: 年逾九十，強壯如五六十者。

translations.literal: Past ninety years of age he was as vigorous as a man of fifty or sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Past ninety he remained as vigorous as a man of fifty or sixty.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，輒先眾到公門。

translations.literal: At every court assembly he always arrived at the official gate before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly he always arrived at the gate before the others.

sentences.zh: 力于仁義，行己過人甚遠。

translations.literal: He exerted himself in benevolence and righteousness; in conduct he surpassed others by far.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to righteousness in conduct that far surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 從兄靈慶嘗病寄謙，謙行出，還問起居，靈慶曰：「向飲冷熱不調，即時猶渴。」

translations.literal: His older cousin Lingqing once fell ill and stayed with Qian; Qian went out on business, returned and asked after his condition; Lingqing said: "Just now I drank something improperly hot or cold and am still thirsty at once."
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lingqing once fell ill while staying with him. Sun Qian went out on business and upon returning asked after him; Lingqing said: "I drank something improperly hot or cold and am still thirsty."

sentences.zh: 謙退遣其妻。

translations.literal: Qian withdrew and sent his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian withdrew and sent his wife to attend to him.

sentences.zh: 有彭城劉融行乞，疾篤無所歸，友人輿送謙舍，謙開聽事以受之。

translations.literal: There was Liu Rong of Pengcheng, a traveling beggar, gravely ill with nowhere to go; a friend carried him in a litter to Qian's house, and Qian opened the reception hall to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: A beggar from Pengcheng named Liu Rong, gravely ill and without shelter, was brought by a friend to Sun Qian's home; Sun Qian opened his reception hall to take him in.

sentences.zh: 及融死，以禮殯葬，眾咸服其行義。

translations.literal: When Rong died he buried him with full rites; the multitude all admired his righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Rong died Sun Qian buried him with full rites, and all admired his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 末年，頭生二肉角，各長一寸。

translations.literal: In his final years two fleshy horns grew on his head, each one inch long.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years two fleshy horns grew on his head, each an inch long.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒官，時年九十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died in office; at the time he was ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died in office at the age of ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺命諸子曰：「吾少無人間意，故自不求聞達，而仕歷三代，官成兩朝，如我資名，或蒙贈諡，自公體耳。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left instructions to his sons, saying: "From youth I had no worldly ambition, and therefore did not seek fame and advancement myself; yet I served through three dynasties and held office under two reigns; for one of my standing and reputation, a posthumous title may perhaps be granted—it is a matter of public propriety.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he instructed his sons: "I never sought worldly fame, yet I served three dynasties and held office under two emperors—for a man of my standing a posthumous title may be granted by custom, but that is a matter for the court.

sentences.zh: 氣絕即以幅巾就葬，每存儉率。

translations.literal: Once breath ceased he was to be buried at once in a headcloth; always preserve frugality and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Once I breathe my last, bury me at once in a simple headcloth, as I have always lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 比見鑐車過精，非吾志也。

translations.literal: Lately I have seen lacquered funeral carriages overly elaborate; this is not my wish.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately seen overly elaborate funeral carriages—that is not my wish.

sentences.zh: 士安束以蘧蒢，王孫裸入後地，雖是匹夫之節，取於人情未允。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji was bound with rushes and reeds, Yang Wangsun entered the earth naked—although these were the principles of common men, they do not accord with human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji was wrapped in rushes for burial and Yang Wangsun was interred naked—though these were the ways of humble men, they do not satisfy ordinary sentiment.

sentences.zh: 今使棺足周身，壙足容柩。

translations.literal: Now let the coffin be only large enough for the body, and the grave only large enough to hold the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Let the coffin be only as long as my body and the grave only large enough to hold it.

sentences.zh: 旐書爵裏，無曰不然。

translations.literal: The funeral pennant and inscribed title on the shroud—do not say it should not be so.
translations.idiomatic: A funeral pennant and inscription of rank on the shroud are acceptable.

sentences.zh: 旒表命數，差可停息。

translations.literal: The mourning streamers and rank insignia may be reduced as much as possible.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning streamers and rank insignia should be kept to a minimum.

sentences.zh: 直僦糯床，裝之以席。

translations.literal: Directly rent a plain bed and line it with a mat for the bier.
translations.idiomatic: Rent a plain bed and line it with a mat for the bier.

sentences.zh: 以常所乘者為魂車，他無所用。」

translations.literal: Use the carriage I ordinarily ride as the soul-cart; nothing else is needed."
translations.idiomatic: Use my usual carriage as the soul-cart and nothing more."

sentences.zh: 第二子貞巧，乃織細席裝鑐，以篾為鈴佩，雖素而華。

translations.literal: His second son Zhenqiao was skillful; he wove a fine mat to wrap the lacquered coffin and made bell pendants from bamboo strips—though plain, yet elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhenqiao, skilled with his hands, wove a fine mat to wrap the coffin and fashioned bamboo strips into bell pendants—simple yet elegant.

sentences.zh: 帝為舉哀，甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned for him and deeply grieved and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and deeply regretted his passing.

sentences.zh: 從子廉字思約。

translations.literal: His nephew Lian, courtesy name Siyue.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Sun Lian, courtesy name Siyue.

sentences.zh: 父奉伯位少府卿、淮南太守。

translations.literal: His father Fengbo held the posts of Minister of the Palace Treasury and Prefect of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Fengbo had served as minister of the palace treasury and governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 廉便辟巧宦，齊時已曆大縣，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Lian was smooth and adept at clever official maneuvering; already in Qi he had passed through major counties and served as Right Assistant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lian was smooth and adept at maneuvering for advancement; under Qi he had already served in major counties and as right assistant in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天監初，沈約、範雲當朝用事，廉傾意奉之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian Shen Yue and Fan Yun held power at court; Lian poured out his intent to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian, when Shen Yue and Fan Yun held power at court, Sun Lian curried favor with them devotedly.

sentences.zh: 及中書舍人黃睦之等，亦尤所結附。

translations.literal: As for Palace Secretariat Attendants such as Huang Muzhi, he also especially cultivated ties with them.
translations.idiomatic: He also cultivated close ties with palace secretaries such as Huang Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 凡貴要每食，廉必日進滋旨，皆手自煎調，不辭勤劇，遂得為列卿，御史中丞，晉陵吳興太守。

translations.literal: Whenever powerful figures dined, Lian always daily presented rich delicacies, all personally fried and prepared by his own hand, not shirking arduous labor; thereby he came to serve as a ranked minister, Censor-in-Chief, and Prefect of Jinling and Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet of the mighty Sun Lian personally prepared and delivered rich delicacies day after day without shirking the labor, and through this rose to ministerial rank, censor-in-chief, and governor of Jinling and Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 廣陵高爽有險薄才，客于廉，廉委以文記。

translations.literal: Gao Shuang of Guangling had a talent for sharp, reckless wit; he lodged with Sun Lian, who entrusted him with literary records.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shuang of Guangling had a gift for barbed wit; he stayed with Sun Lian, who put him in charge of official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 爽嘗有求不遂，乃為屐謎以喻廉曰：「刺鼻不知嚏，蹋面不知嗔，齧齒作步數，持此得勝人。」

translations.literal: Once Shuang had a request denied, he made a riddle about clogs to mock Lian, saying: "A stinging nose but no sneeze; a stomped face but no anger; gnawing teeth to count steps—with such things one beats others."
translations.idiomatic: When a request of his went unsatisfied, Shuang devised a clog riddle aimed at Lian: "A nose pricked but no sneeze; a face stepped on but no rage; teeth gnawing to keep count of steps—live like that and you will rise above others."

sentences.zh: 譏其不計恥辱，以此取名位。

translations.literal: It mocked him for not counting shame and disgrace, and so winning name and rank by it.
translations.idiomatic: It mocked Lian for swallowing every humiliation to climb the ladder of office.

sentences.zh: 然處官平直，遂以善政稱。

translations.literal: Yet in office he was upright and fair, and was therefore praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in office he was upright and fair, and earned a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗曰：「東莞二孫，謙、廉而已。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once said: "Of the two Suns of Dongguan, only Qian and Lian deserve mention."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once said, "Among the Suns of Dongguan, only Sun Qian and Sun Lian are worth remembering."

sentences.zh: 何遠字義方，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Yuan, styled Yifang, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Yuan, styled Yifang, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慧炬，齊尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Huiju was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huiju had served as a master of writing under Qi.

sentences.zh: 遠仕齊為奉朝請，豫崔慧景敗亡事，抵尚書令蕭懿，懿深保匿焉。

translations.literal: Yuan served Qi as a Court Attendant; he took part in Cui Huijing's defeat and flight, and was sent to the Masters of Writing Chief Xiao Yi, who deeply protected and hid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served Qi as a court attendant and was implicated in Cui Huijing's rebellion; though handed over to chief minister Xiao Yi, Yi took him under deep protection.

sentences.zh: 會赦出。

translations.literal: By chance an amnesty freed him.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty eventually freed him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，懿遭難，子弟皆潛伏，遠求得懿弟融藏之。

translations.literal: Soon Yi met disaster; his sons and younger kinsmen all went into hiding; Yuan found Yi's younger brother Rong and hid him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yi met disaster; his sons and kinsmen went into hiding, and Yuan found Yi's younger brother Rong and concealed him.

sentences.zh: 既而發覺，遠踰垣以免，融遇禍，遠家屬系尚方。

translations.literal: When this came to light, Yuan vaulted the wall to escape; Rong met disaster, and Yuan's family were imprisoned at the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: When this was discovered, Yuan scaled a wall to escape; Rong was killed, and Yuan's family were sent to the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 遠遂亡度江，因降魏。

translations.literal: Yuan then fled across the Yangzi and submitted to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan fled south across the Yangzi and defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 入壽陽見刺史王肅，求迎梁武帝，肅遣兵援送。

translations.literal: He entered Shouyang and saw Prefect Wang Su, asking to welcome the Liang Emperor of Martial Propriety; Su sent troops to escort and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shouyang he met prefect Wang Su and asked to be sent to welcome the future Emperor Wu of Liang; Su dispatched troops to escort him back.

sentences.zh: 武帝見遠謂張弘策曰：「何遠丈夫，而能破家報舊德，未易及也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu saw Yuan he said to Zhang Hongce: "He Yuan is a true man—able to ruin his family to repay old kindness; not easy to match."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu met Yuan he told Zhang Hongce, "He Yuan is a man of mettle—he risked ruin of his house to repay an old debt of kindness. Not many could do that."

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，以奉迎勳，封廣興男，為後軍鄱陽王恢錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, for the merit of welcoming him he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangxing and made Recorder of the Prince of Poyang, Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yuan was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangxing for helping welcome him and appointed recorder to Prince Hui of Poyang of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 遠與恢素善，在府盡其志力，知無不為。

translations.literal: Yuan and Hui had long been on good terms; in the princely household he gave his full will and strength, and whenever he knew something needed doing he did it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Prince Hui had been close for years; in the princely household he gave all he had and left nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 恢亦推心仗之，恩寄甚密。

translations.literal: Hui also opened his heart and relied on him; favor and trust were very close.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui in turn trusted him completely; their bond was unusually close.

sentences.zh: 遷武昌太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 遠本倜儻，尚輕俠。

translations.literal: Yuan had originally been free-spirited and fond of swashbuckling ways.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had always been bold and fond of the freewheeling life.

sentences.zh: 至是乃折節為吏，杜絕交遊，饋遺秋毫無所受。

translations.literal: From then he restrained himself to serve as an official, cut off social contacts, and accepted not a hair's breadth in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sobered into official life, cut off his old circle, and refused the smallest gift.

sentences.zh: 武昌俗皆汲江水，盛夏，遠患水溫，每以錢買人井寒水。

translations.literal: In Wuchang the custom was to draw water from the Yangzi; in midsummer Yuan disliked the warm water and each day paid cash to buy people's well water, cold.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang folk drew their drinking water from the Yangzi; in midsummer Yuan found it too warm and each day paid people for cold well water.

sentences.zh: 不取錢者，則摙水還之，其他事率多如此。

translations.literal: Those who would take no payment he gave the water back to; most other matters were much the same.
translations.idiomatic: If someone refused payment, he returned the water; in most such matters he acted the same way.

sentences.zh: 跡雖似偽，而能委曲用意。

translations.literal: The trace may seem feigned, yet he could bend circumstances to his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The performance looked like theatre, yet he meant every courtesy in it.

sentences.zh: 車服尤弊素，器物無銅漆。

translations.literal: His carriage and robes were especially plain and worn; his utensils had neither bronze nor lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: His carriage and robes were threadbare; his household goods were plain wood, without bronze fittings or lacquer.

sentences.zh: 江左水族甚賤，遠每食不過幹魚數片而已。

translations.literal: In the lands south of the Yangzi aquatic foods were very cheap; Yuan's meals never exceeded a few slices of dried fish.
translations.idiomatic: Fish was cheap in the south, and Yuan's meals were no more than a few strips of dried fish.

sentences.zh: 然性剛嚴，吏人多以細事受鞭罰，遂為人所訟，征下廷尉，被劾十數條。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stern and severe; clerks often received flogging over petty matters, so people sued him, and he was summoned to the Minister of Justice and charged with more than ten counts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was harsh by nature, and clerks were often flogged over petty faults; he was denounced, summoned before the minister of justice, and charged on more than ten counts.

sentences.zh: 當時士大夫坐法皆不受測，遠度己無贓，就測立三七日不款，猶以私藏禁仗除名。

translations.literal: At that time gentry and officials charged with crimes all refused examination; Yuan judged himself free of bribery, submitted to examination, and stood twenty-seven days without confessing, yet was still stripped of rank for privately hoarding forbidden weapons.
translations.idiomatic: At the time educated officials charged with crimes usually refused interrogation; believing himself innocent of bribery, Yuan submitted to questioning and held out twenty-seven days without confessing, yet still lost his post for keeping forbidden weapons in private.

sentences.zh: 後為武康令，愈厲廉節，除淫祀，正身率職，人甚稱之。

translations.literal: Later he was Magistrate of Wukang, further strict in integrity, abolished illicit cults, corrected his person and led his duties—the people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Wukang, he was fiercer still about integrity; he suppressed illicit cults, led by example, and the people praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 太守王彬巡屬縣，諸縣皆盛供帳以待焉。

translations.literal: Administrator Wang Bin toured the dependent counties; every county set up lavish supplies and tents to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When administrator Wang Bin toured the subordinate counties, each one laid out lavish feasts and tents to receive him.

sentences.zh: 至武康，遠獨設糗水而已。

translations.literal: Reaching Wukang, Yuan alone set out only parched grain and water.
translations.idiomatic: At Wukang, Yuan offered only parched grain and plain water.

sentences.zh: 彬去，遠送至境，進鬥酒只鵝而別。

translations.literal: When Bin left, Yuan saw him to the border and presented one dou of wine and one goose in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin departed, Yuan saw him to the commandery border and sent him off with a pint of wine and a single goose.

sentences.zh: 彬戲曰：「卿禮有過陸納，將不為古人所笑乎。」

translations.literal: Bin joked: "Your courtesy surpasses Lu Na's; will you not be laughed at by men of old?'
translations.idiomatic: Bin teased him, "Your hospitality puts Lu Na to shame—aren't you afraid the ancients would laugh at you?'

sentences.zh: 武帝聞其能，擢為宣城太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of his ability and promoted him to Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of his conduct and promoted him to administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 自縣為近畿大郡，近代未之有也。

translations.literal: From magistrate to a great commandery of the near capital—nothing of the kind in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: A leap from county magistrate to a great commandery near the capital was unheard of in recent times.

sentences.zh: 郡經寇抄，遠盡心綏理，復著名跡。

translations.literal: The commandery had suffered raids and plunder; Yuan with all his heart settled and restored it, and his fame was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had been ravaged by bandits; Yuan worked tirelessly to restore order and rebuilt his reputation.

sentences.zh: 期年，遷樹功將軍、始興內史。

translations.literal: Within a year he was transferred to General Who Establishes Merit and Inner Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was made general who establishes merit and inner administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時泉陵侯朗為桂州，緣道多剽掠，入始興界，草木無所犯。

translations.literal: At that time Marquis Quanling Lang was Prefect of Guizhou; along the route there was much pillaging, but entering the borders of Shixing, no grass or tree was touched.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Marquis Quanling Lang was governor of Guizhou; his route was notorious for pillage, yet in Shixing not a blade of grass was disturbed.

sentences.zh: 遠在官好開途巷，修葺牆屋，人居市里，城隍廄庫，所過若營家焉。

translations.literal: Yuan in office loved to open roads and lanes and repair walls and houses; dwellings in markets and wards, city walls, stables, and storehouses—wherever he passed it was as if tending his own home.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yuan loved opening new streets and repairing walls and houses; markets, city walls, stables, and storehouses alike were treated as if they were his own household.

sentences.zh: 田秩奉錢，並無所取，歲暮擇人尤窮者充其租調，以此為常。

translations.literal: Field allotments and salary stipends he took none of; at year's end he chose the most destitute people to fill their tax and dues levies—this he made his custom.
translations.idiomatic: He took none of his field income or salary supplements; at year's end he routinely paid the tax quotas of the poorest people himself.

sentences.zh: 然其聽訟猶人也，不能過絕。

translations.literal: Yet in hearing lawsuits he was still like other men, and could not break utterly from custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in court he was still human—he could not be utterly above favor and partiality.

sentences.zh: 而性果斷，人畏而惜之，所至皆生為立祠，表言政狀，帝每優詔答焉。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was resolute; men both feared and cherished him; wherever he went living shrines were built for him, memorials praised his governance, and the Emperor each time answered with gracious edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was decisive by nature; people feared yet admired him; wherever he served, living shrines were raised in his honor and petitions praised his rule, and the emperor answered each time with generous edicts.

sentences.zh: 後曆給事黃門侍郎，信武將軍，監吳郡。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Trustworthy Martial General, and overseer of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, trustworthy martial general, and supervisor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 在吳頗有酒失。

translations.literal: In Wu he had rather many lapses owing to wine.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu he had a few too many drunken missteps.

sentences.zh: 遷東陽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 遠處職，疾強富如仇讎，視貧細如子弟，特為豪右所畏憚。

translations.literal: Yuan in office hated the mighty rich as if they were sworn foes, treated the poor and humble as if they were sons and younger kinsmen, and was especially feared by the powerful clans.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yuan treated the powerful rich like enemies, the poor and humble like family, and was especially feared by the local magnates.

sentences.zh: 在東陽歲餘，復為受罰者所謗，坐免歸。

translations.literal: In Dongyang for more than a year, again those he had punished slandered him; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year in Dongyang, those he had punished denounced him again; he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 遠性耿介，無私曲，居人間絕請謁，不造詣。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was upright and unbending, without private bias; among men he cut off petitions and visits, and paid no calls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was upright and incorruptible; he accepted no petitions or callers and never paid social visits.

sentences.zh: 與貴賤書疏，抗禮如一。

translations.literal: In letters with the noble and base he held his etiquette equal throughout.
translations.idiomatic: In correspondence with high and low alike he maintained the same respectful distance.

sentences.zh: 其所會遇，未嘗以顏色下人。

translations.literal: In every meeting he never lowered his bearing toward others.
translations.idiomatic: In every encounter he refused to soften his manner for anyone's sake.

sentences.zh: 是以多為俗士所疾惡。

translations.literal: Therefore he was often hated by vulgar gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason vulgar men often despised him.

sentences.zh: 其清公實為天下第一。

translations.literal: His purity and public-mindedness were in truth first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was in truth unmatched anywhere under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 居數郡，見可欲終不變其心，妻子饑寒如下貧者。

translations.literal: Holding several commanderies, when he saw desirable things his heart never changed; wife and children hungered and froze like the poorest.
translations.idiomatic: Through several commanderies, temptation never moved him; his wife and children went hungry and cold like the poorest families.

sentences.zh: 及去東陽歸家，經年歲，口不言榮辱，士類益以此多之。

translations.literal: After leaving Dongyang and returning home, for years he spoke not of honor or disgrace; the gentry all the more thought well of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving Dongyang and returning home, he spoke of neither glory nor shame for years; cultivated men admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 其輕財好義，周人之急，言不虛妄，蓋天性也。

translations.literal: His light regard for wealth and love of righteousness, relieving others in urgency, speech without falsehood—these were his nature.
translations.idiomatic: His disregard for money, his love of justice, his aid to the desperate, his truthfulness—these were his nature.

sentences.zh: 每戲語人云：「卿能得我一妄語，則謝卿以一縑。」

translations.literal: He often jestingly told people: "If you can catch me in one false word, I will thank you with a bolt of silk."
translations.idiomatic: He often joked, "If you can catch me in a lie, I'll give you a bolt of silk.'

sentences.zh: 眾共伺之，不能記也。

translations.literal: The crowd together watched for this, but could not record one.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone tried, but no one could cite one.

sentences.zh: 後為征西諮議參軍、中撫軍司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Staff Advisor to the Western Expedition and Marshal of the Central Pacification Army, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as staff advisor to the western expedition and marshal of the central pacification army, then died.

sentences.zh: 郭祖深，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Guo Zushen was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zushen came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝初起，以客從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang first rose, Zushen followed him as a retainer guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang first rose, Zushen followed him as a client.

sentences.zh: 後隨蔡道恭在司州。

translations.literal: Later he followed Cai Daogong in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served under Cai Daogong in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 陷北還，上書言境上事，不見用。

translations.literal: After the north fell he returned, submitted a memorial on border matters, and was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: After the northern territories were lost he returned and submitted a memorial on border affairs, but it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 選為長兼南梁郡丞，徙後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: He was selected to serve concurrently as Assistant of Nanliang Commandery, then transferred to Rear Army Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen as concurrent assistant administrator of Nanliang commandery, then made a staff officer of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 帝溺情內教，朝政縱弛，祖深輿櫬詣闕上封事，其略曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor was drowned in affection for inner teachings; court governance grew slack; Zushen carried his coffin to the palace gates and submitted a sealed memorial; its gist said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lost himself in Buddhist devotion and court discipline slackened; Zushen carried a coffin to the palace gates and submitted a sealed memorial that read, in part:

sentences.zh: 大梁應運，功高百王，慈悲既弘，憲律如替。

translations.literal: Great Liang received the Mandate; its merit surpasses the hundred kings; mercy is already broad, but statutes and laws seem cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Great Liang received Heaven's mandate; its achievements surpass those of a hundred kings, yet as compassion has grown boundless, law has been left to wither.

sentences.zh: 愚輩罔識，褫慢斯作。

translations.literal: The foolish know nothing; insolence and disrespect arise.
translations.idiomatic: The foolish no longer know their place, and insolence flourishes.

sentences.zh: 各競奢侈，貪穢遂生。

translations.literal: Each races in luxury; greed and foulness are born.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone races toward extravagance, and greed and corruption follow.

sentences.zh: 頗由陛下寵勳太過，馭下太寬，故廉潔者自進無途，貪苛者取入多徑，直弦者淪溺溝壑，曲鉤者升進重遝。

translations.literal: Much because Your Majesty favors merit too greatly and governs subordinates too loosely—thus the honest find no road to advance themselves, the greedy and harsh have many paths of gain, the straight string sinks drowned in gullies, the crooked hook rises and rises again.
translations.idiomatic: This stems in part from Your Majesty's excessive favor for meritorious men and excessive lenience toward subordinates: the honest have no path to advancement, the greedy many routes to profit, the upright sink into obscurity, and the crooked climb again and again.

sentences.zh: 飾口利辭，競相推薦，訥直守信，坐見埋沒。

translations.literal: Polished mouths and clever words compete in mutual recommendation; slow-spoken, straight, and faithful men sit by and are buried.
translations.idiomatic: Smooth talkers compete to recommend one another, while blunt, honest men are left buried in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 勞深勳厚，祿賞未均，無功側入，反加寵擢。

translations.literal: Labor deep and merit thick, salary and reward not equal; the meritless sidle in and instead receive favor and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Those with deep service and heavy merit go unrewarded, while the undeserving slip in and win even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 昔宋人賣酒，犬惡致酸，陛下之犬，其甚矣哉。

translations.literal: In old times a Song man sold wine; the dog's hatred made it sour; Your Majesty's dog—how very much so!
translations.idiomatic: Once a wine seller in Song found his wine turned sour because his dog barked at customers—Your Majesty's dogs have grown even worse!

sentences.zh: 臣聞人為國本，食為人命，故禮曰國無六年之儲，謂非其國也。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that the people are the root of the state and food is the life of the people; thus the Ritual says a state without six years' stores is not a true state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the people are the root of the state and food the lifeblood of the people; the Book of Rites says a state without six years' reserves is no true state at all.

sentences.zh: 推此而言，農為急務。

translations.literal: Extending from this to speak, agriculture is the urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: By that reckoning, agriculture is the urgent task.

sentences.zh: 而郡縣苛暴，不加勸獎，今年豐歲稔，猶人有饑色，設遇水旱，何以救之？

translations.literal: Yet commanderies and counties are harsh and violent, and give no encouragement; this year the harvest is rich and ripe, yet people still show the color of hunger—if flood or drought come, with what will you save them?
translations.idiomatic: Yet commanderies and counties are harsh and offer no encouragement to farming; this year the harvest is abundant, yet people still look hungry—if flood or drought strike, how will you save them?

sentences.zh: 陛下昔歲尚學，置立五館，行吟坐詠，誦聲溢境。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in former years honored learning, established the five halls, chanting while walking, intoning while sitting—recitation voices overflowed the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once honored learning, established the five halls of study, and filled the realm with chanting voices wherever scholars walked or sat.

sentences.zh: 比來慕法，普天信向，家家齋戒，人人懺禮，不務農桑，空談彼岸。

translations.literal: Recently admiring the Dharma, all under Heaven believe and turn; every house keeps fasts, every person performs repentance rites—not tending agriculture or sericulture, vainly talking of the far shore.
translations.idiomatic: Lately all under Heaven have turned to Buddhism—every household keeps fasts, every soul performs repentance—and neglects farming and weaving for empty talk of nirvana.

sentences.zh: 夫農桑者今日濟育，功德者將來勝因，豈可墮本勤末，置邇效賒也。

translations.literal: Agriculture and sericulture nourish today; meritorious deeds are the superior cause of the future—how can one abandon the root and toil at the branch, set near effects aside and defer distant ones?
translations.idiomatic: Farming and weaving feed us today; merit may bear fruit tomorrow—but how can you abandon the root to chase the branch, neglect the present for a distant reward?

sentences.zh: 今商旅轉繁，遊食轉眾，耕夫日少，杼軸日空。

translations.literal: Now merchants and travelers grow ever more numerous, wandering eaters ever more many; tillers grow fewer day by day, shuttles and looms grow empty day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and travelers multiply; idlers on the road multiply; farmers dwindle daily and looms stand idle.

sentences.zh: 陛下若廣興屯田，賤金貴粟，勤農桑者擢以階級，惰耕織者告以明刑。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty broadly promote military colonies, cheapen gold and honor grain, promote those diligent in agriculture and sericulture by ranks and grades, and announce clear punishments to those idle in tilling and weaving—
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty broadly expanded military colonies, made grain dear and gold cheap, promoted the diligent farmer, and punished the idle weaver with clear penalties—

sentences.zh: 如此數年，則家給人足，廉讓可生。

translations.literal: Thus for several years, then households would be provided and the people satisfied, and integrity and yielding could arise.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years households would be full and the people content, and modesty and justice would flourish again.

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人，智計不同，君子志于道，小人謀於利。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and petty men differ in wisdom and design—the gentleman sets his will on the Way, the petty man schemes for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and petty men think differently: the gentleman aims at the Way, the petty man at profit.

sentences.zh: 志于道者安國濟人，志於利者損物圖己。

translations.literal: He who sets his will on the Way settles the state and saves the people; he who sets his will on profit harms things and schemes for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He who seeks the Way steadies the state and helps the people; he who seeks profit harms the realm and enriches himself.

sentences.zh: 道人者害國小人也，忠良者捍國君子也。

translations.literal: Daoist masters are petty men who harm the state; loyal and good men are gentlemen who defend the state.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist monks are petty men who harm the state; loyal worthies are gentlemen who defend it.

sentences.zh: 臣見疾者詣道士則勸奏章，僧尼則令齋講，俗師則鬼禍須解，醫診則湯熨散丸，皆先自為也。

translations.literal: Your servant sees the sick visit Daoist masters and are urged to submit memorial petitions; monks and nuns order fasting lectures; lay shamans say ghost disasters must be resolved; physicians prescribe decoctions, cautery, powders, and pills—all doing for themselves first.
translations.idiomatic: I see the sick visit Daoist priests who urge ritual petitions, monks and nuns who order fasts and sermons, lay shamans who demand exorcism of ghostly harm, and physicians who prescribe brews and pills—all serving themselves first.

sentences.zh: 臣謂為國之本，與療病相類，療病當去巫鬼，尋華、扁，為國當黜佞邪，用管、晏。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the root of governing the state is similar to treating illness—treating illness one should remove shamans and ghosts and seek Hua Tuo and Bian Que; governing the state one should dismiss flatterers and the wicked and employ Guan Zhong and Yan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that governing a state is like treating illness: heal the sick by driving out shamans and calling in healers like Hua Tuo and Bian Que; govern the realm by removing sycophants and employing ministers like Guan Zhong and Yan Ying.

sentences.zh: 今之所任，腹背之毛耳。

translations.literal: Those now appointed are only the hairs on belly and back.
translations.idiomatic: Those you appoint today are trifles—hairs on an ox's belly and back.

sentences.zh: 論外則有勉、舍，說內則有雲、旻。

translations.literal: In discussing foreign affairs there are Mian and She; in advising the inner court there are Yun and Min.
translations.idiomatic: On foreign affairs you listen to Mian and She; at court you heed Yun and Min.

sentences.zh: 雲、旻所議則傷俗盛法，勉、舍之志唯願安枕江東。

translations.literal: What Yun and Min discuss harms custom and exalts the Dharma; Mian and She's aim is only to sleep easy east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Min would let custom wither and exalt Buddhist law; Mian and She care only to sleep secure east of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 主慈臣恇，息謀外甸，使中國士女南望懷冤，若賈誼重生，豈不慟哭。

translations.literal: The ruler is kindly and ministers are timid; plots for the outer domains cease, making the gentry and women of the central lands look south with stored grievance—if Jia Yi were reborn, would he not wail in grief?
translations.idiomatic: A kindly emperor and timid ministers have abandoned plans for the northern territories, leaving the people of the heartland gazing south with bitter grief—if Jia Yi lived again, would he not weep?

sentences.zh: 臣今直言犯顏，罪或容宥，而乖忤貴臣，則禍在不測。

translations.literal: Your servant now speaks bluntly and offends your countenance; pardon for crime may perhaps be granted, but to oppose great ministers brings disaster beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: I speak bluntly now and risk your wrath; you may forgive the offense, but if I cross powerful ministers the consequences are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 所以不憚鼎鑊區區必聞者，正以社稷計重而螻蟻命輕。

translations.literal: The reason I do not fear the cauldron and merely insist on being heard is precisely that I take the altars of soil and grain as weighty and an ant's life as light.
translations.idiomatic: I dare the cauldron only because the fate of the state matters more than the life of one man.

sentences.zh: 使臣言入身滅，臣何所恨。

translations.literal: If my words enter and my person perishes, what would Your servant regret?
translations.idiomatic: If my words are heard and I die for them, what would I regret?

sentences.zh: 夫謀臣良將，何代無之，貴在見知，要在用耳。

translations.literal: Planning ministers and good generals—what age lacks them? Precious is to be known; crucial is to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Every age has its strategists and good generals; what matters is to recognize them—and then use them.

sentences.zh: 陛下皇基兆運二十餘載，臣子之節，諫爭是誰？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's imperial foundation has been rising for more than twenty years—among the integrity of ministers and sons, who has remonstrated?
translations.idiomatic: Your imperial foundation has stood for more than twenty years—who among your ministers has truly remonstrated with you?

sentences.zh: 執事皆同而不和，答問唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Those in charge are all alike but not in harmony; in answer they only murmur agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Those in office echo one another without honest debate; their answers are nothing but "yes, yes."

sentences.zh: 入對則言聖旨神衷，出論則雲誰敢逆耳。

translations.literal: Facing in they speak of holy intent and divine heart; going out they say who dares oppose the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Before you they praise your divine will; outside they ask who would dare speak against it.

sentences.zh: 過實在下而謫見於上，遂使聖皇降誠，躬自引咎，宰輔晏然，曾無謙退。

translations.literal: Fault in truth lies below yet reproof appears above; thus the sage Emperor lowers sincerity and personally accepts blame, while chief ministers remain serene and never yield or step back.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies below yet rebuke falls on you; so the sage emperor humbles himself and accepts blame, while the chief ministers sit untouched, never yielding an inch.

sentences.zh: 且百僚卿士，少有奉公，屍祿競利，不尚廉潔。

translations.literal: Moreover among the hundred officials and ministers few serve the public; corpse-salary men compete for profit and do not honor integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among the hundred officials few serve the public; most hold empty posts, scramble for profit, and scorn integrity.

sentences.zh: 累金積鏹，侍列如仙，不田不商，何故而爾？

translations.literal: Amassing gold and hoarding coin, attendants rank like immortals—neither farming nor trading; for what reason are they thus?
translations.idiomatic: They pile up gold and silver, stand in court like immortals, yet neither farm nor trade—how do they grow so rich?

sentences.zh: 法者人之父母，惠者人之仇讎，法嚴則人思善，德多則物生惡，惡不可長，欲不可縱。

translations.literal: Law is the people's parent; favor is the people's enemy—strict law makes people think of goodness; much virtue makes things breed evil; evil must not be lengthened; desire must not be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Law is the people's protector; indulgence is their enemy—strict law makes men good, while too much mercy breeds vice; evil must not be indulged, desire must not be unchecked.

sentences.zh: 伏願去貪濁，進廉平，明法令，嚴刑罰，禁奢侈，薄賦斂，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that greed and foulness be removed, integrity and fairness be advanced, laws and edicts be clarified, punishments be strict, luxury be forbidden, and tax levies be lightened—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that you purge corruption, promote the honest, clarify the laws, enforce stern punishments, forbid extravagance, and lighten taxes—then all under Heaven would rejoice.

sentences.zh: 謹上封事二十九條，伏願抑獨斷之明，少察愚瞽。

translations.literal: Respectfully submitting twenty-nine sealed memorial items; prostrate, Your servant wishes that the brilliance of solitary judgment be moderated, and that this blind and deaf fool be given a little consideration.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit twenty-nine sealed memorial items, and beg that Your Majesty temper the brilliance of sole authority and spare a little attention for this blind fool.

sentences.zh: 時帝大弘釋典，將以易俗，故祖深尤言其事，條以為：

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor greatly promoted Buddhist scriptures, intending thereby to change popular customs; therefore Zushen especially spoke of this matter, set it forth in numbered points as follows:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then greatly promoting Buddhist scripture, intending to transform society through it; so Zushen spoke at length on the subject and laid out his points:

sentences.zh: 都下佛寺五百餘所，窮極宏麗。

translations.literal: In the capital there are more than five hundred Buddhist temples, magnificence pushed to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital alone stand more than five hundred Buddhist temples, each one extravagantly grand.

sentences.zh: 僧尼十餘萬，資產豐沃。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns number more than a hundred thousand; their assets are abundant and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns exceed a hundred thousand in number, their wealth ample beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 所在郡縣，不可勝言。

translations.literal: In every commandery and county, it cannot be told in full.
translations.idiomatic: In every commandery and county the like defies description.

sentences.zh: 道人又有白徒，尼則皆畜養女，皆不貫人籍，天下戶口幾亡其半。

translations.literal: Buddhist monks also have white followers; nuns all keep foster-girls—all are not entered on household registers; the registered population of all under Heaven has nearly lost half.
translations.idiomatic: Monks keep unregistered "white followers," and nuns foster young women—none appear on the census rolls; nearly half the empire's registered households have vanished from the books.

sentences.zh: 而僧尼多非法，養女皆服羅紈，其蠹俗傷法，抑由於此。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns are largely unlawful; foster-girls all wear silk gauze—the corruption of custom and injury to law stem chiefly from this.
translations.idiomatic: Most monks and nuns live outside the law; their foster-girls dress in silk—the rot in custom and the damage to law begin here.

sentences.zh: 請精加檢括，若無道行，四十已下，皆使還俗附農。

translations.literal: I ask that careful investigation be applied; those without cultivation of the Way, all below forty, be made to return to lay life and be attached to farming.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that rigorous inspection be carried out: those without true spiritual attainment, all under forty, should be returned to lay life and put to farming.

sentences.zh: 罷白徒養女，聽畜奴婢。

translations.literal: Abolish white followers and foster-girls; allow keeping of male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish white followers and foster-girls, and permit monasteries to keep only proper servants.

sentences.zh: 婢唯著青布衣，僧尼皆令蔬食。

translations.literal: Slave-girls may wear only green-blue plain cloth; monks and nuns should all be ordered to eat vegetarian food.
translations.idiomatic: Servants may wear only plain blue cloth; monks and nuns must eat nothing but vegetables.

sentences.zh: 如此，則法興俗盛，國富人殷。

translations.literal: If so, the Dharma would flourish and custom thrive; the state would be rich and the people abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Dharma would flourish, custom would thrive, and the realm would grow rich and the people prosperous.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐方來處處成寺，家家剃落，尺土一人，非復國有。

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear in the time to come temples will rise everywhere, every household will take tonsure—one person per foot of soil—and the land would no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear a day when every corner holds a temple and every household shaves its head—one monk per foot of soil—and the realm itself would cease to exist.

sentences.zh: 朝廷擢用勳舊，為三陲州郡，不顧御人之道，唯以貪殘為務。

translations.literal: The court selects and employs meritorious old officials for the three frontier commanderies and districts, heedless of the Way of governing the people, seeking only greed and cruelty as their task.
translations.idiomatic: The court appoints veteran merit-holders to the three frontier regions, men who ignore the art of governing and devote themselves only to greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 迫脅良善，害甚豺狼。

translations.literal: They coerce and threaten the good; their harm exceeds wolves.
translations.idiomatic: They bully the honest and do worse harm than wolves.

sentences.zh: 江、湘人尤受其弊。

translations.literal: The people of the Jiang and Xiang regions especially suffer their harm.
translations.idiomatic: The people along the Yangzi and Xiang rivers suffer their abuses most of all.

sentences.zh: 自三關以外，是處遭毒。

translations.literal: Beyond the Three Passes, everywhere suffers their poison.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Three Passes, every district feels their poison.

sentences.zh: 而此勳人投化之始，但有一身，及被任用，皆募部曲。

translations.literal: These meritorious men when they first submitted had only their own bodies; once appointed to office, they all recruit military retainers.
translations.idiomatic: When these merit-holders first submitted to the dynasty, they brought nothing but themselves; once appointed, each recruited a private retinue.

sentences.zh: 而揚、徐之人，逼以眾役，多投其募，利其貨財。

translations.literal: The people of Yang and Xu, pressed by the many corvées, mostly join their recruitment, craving their wealth and goods.
translations.idiomatic: People in Yang and Xu provinces, crushed under public labor levies, flock to enlist under them, drawn by their wealth.

sentences.zh: 皆虛名上簿，止送出三津，名在遠役，身歸鄉里。

translations.literal: All are falsely registered on the rolls, merely escorted to the Three Fords; their names are on distant service while their bodies return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: They are falsely entered on the rolls, marched only as far as the Three Fords, then listed as serving afar while in fact they go home.

sentences.zh: 又懼本屬檢問，於是逃亡他境，僑戶之興，良由此故。

translations.literal: Also fearing inquiry by their home districts, they flee to other regions—the rise of floating migrant households owes much to this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing investigation by their native districts, they flee abroad—this is the very source of the floating-household plague.

sentences.zh: 又梁興以來，發人征役，號為三五。

translations.literal: Further, since Liang's rise, men have been conscripted for corvée and military service, called the "three-five."
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Liang, men have been conscripted under the so-called "three-five" levy system.

sentences.zh: 及投募將客，主將無恩，存恤失理，多有物故，輒刺叛亡。

translations.literal: When joining recruited military retainers and guest-soldiers, the commander shows no kindness; care and relief are wrongly administered; many die, yet they are immediately marked as rebel deserters.
translations.idiomatic: Those who enlist as military retainers find their commanders merciless and care disgracefully administered; many die, yet are at once branded deserters and rebels.

sentences.zh: 或有身殞戰場，而名在叛目，監符下討，稱為逋叛，錄質家丁。

translations.literal: Some die on the battlefield yet their names appear on rebel lists; supervisory edicts descend for pursuit, calling them absconding deserters, and family members are taken as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Some fall on the battlefield while their names remain on deserter rolls; pursuit orders go out calling them runaway rebels, and their families are seized as hostages.

sentences.zh: 闔家又叛，則取同籍，同籍又叛，則取比伍，比伍又叛，則望村而取。

translations.literal: If the whole household is again marked rebel, men of the same register are taken; if the same register rebels again, mutual-responsibility groups of five are taken; if the five-household groups rebel again, they seize by whole village.
translations.idiomatic: If the whole household is again listed as rebel, men of the same register are taken; if the register fails again, the five-household group is taken; if that too fails, they sweep up an entire village.

sentences.zh: 一人有犯，則合村皆空。

translations.literal: One man's offense empties a whole village.
translations.idiomatic: One man's fault can depopulate an entire village.

sentences.zh: 雖肆眚時降，蕩滌惟始，而監符猶下舊日，限以嚴程。

translations.literal: Though general amnesties are issued from time to time and lists are cleared only at the start, supervisory edicts still follow old accounts, set with strict deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Though general amnesties come from time to time and the lists are wiped clean at first, supervisory orders still pursue old cases under punishing deadlines.

sentences.zh: 上不任信下，轉相督促。

translations.literal: Superiors do not trust and rely on subordinates, who in turn press one another.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors trust no one below them, and each level drives the next.

sentences.zh: 台使到州，州又遣押使至郡，州郡競急切，同趣下城。

translations.literal: Court envoys reach the province; the province sends escort envoys to the commandery; provinces and commanderies compete in urgency, all rushing to the subordinate cities.
translations.idiomatic: When court envoys arrive at the province, the province sends press-men to the commandery; province and commandery vie in urgency, all descending together on the counties.

sentences.zh: 令宰多庸才，望風畏伏。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are mostly mediocrities; at mere rumor of authority they cringe in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Most magistrates are mediocrities who crumple at the first whiff of authority.

sentences.zh: 於是斂戶課，薦其筐篚，使人納重貨，許立空文。

translations.literal: Then they levy household taxes, display their baskets and hampers, make people pay heavy bribes, and permit empty paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: They levy household taxes, parade their gift baskets, squeeze out heavy bribes, and accept hollow paperwork in return.

sentences.zh: 其百里微欲矯俗，則嚴科立至，自是所在恣意貪利，以事上官。

translations.literal: If a district magistrate slightly wishes to reform custom, harsh penalties arrive at once; from this all everywhere greedily seize profit to serve superiors.
translations.idiomatic: If a district magistrate so much as tries to reform local abuses, harsh penalties follow at once; from then on officials everywhere plunder freely to please their superiors.

sentences.zh: 又「請斷界首將生口入北，及關津廢替，須加糾擿」；

translations.literal: Also: "I ask that frontier commanders be stopped from sending captives northward, and that abandoned border checkpoints be strictly investigated and exposed";
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Stop frontier generals from sending captives north; tighten oversight of abandoned border posts and cross-checks";

sentences.zh: 又言：「廬陵年少，不宜鎮襄陽；

translations.literal: He also said: "The Prince of Luling is young and unsuited to guard Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: He also declared: "The Prince of Luling is too young to hold Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 左僕射王暕在喪，被起為吳郡，曾無辭讓」。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Yan is in mourning yet was recalled to serve as Administrator of Wu commandery, without the least declining."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Yan is in mourning, yet was summoned to govern Wu commandery without a word of refusal."

sentences.zh: 其言深刻。

translations.literal: His words were penetrating and deep.
translations.idiomatic: His words cut deep.

sentences.zh: 又「請復郊四星」。

translations.literal: He also requested, "Restore the four stars of the suburban sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: He also requested, "Restore the four stars of the suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能悉用，然嘉其正直，擢為豫章鍾陵令，員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor could not adopt all of it, he admired his forthrightness and promoted him to Magistrate of Zhongling in Yuzhang, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not adopt all his advice, but admired his honesty and promoted him to Magistrate of Zhongling in Yuzhang commandery, with the additional title of Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，改南州津為南津校尉，以祖深為之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, South Province Ford was changed to South Ford Commandant, with Zushen appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong (526), the South Province Ford post was renamed South Ford Commandant, and Zushen was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 加雲騎將軍，秩二千石。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Cloud Cavalry General, rank of two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title Cloud Cavalry General, at the two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 使募部曲二千。

translations.literal: He was ordered to recruit two thousand military retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was authorized to recruit two thousand personal troops.

sentences.zh: 及至南州，公嚴清刻。

translations.literal: When he reached South Province, he was public-spirited, stern, pure, and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post, he governed with public-minded severity, purity, and exacting discipline.

sentences.zh: 由來王侯勢家出入津，不忌憲綱，俠藏亡命。

translations.literal: Formerly princes, marquises, and powerful families passing through the ford did not fear statutes and regulations; men of force harbored fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Long accustomed to passing the ford with impunity, princes and powerful families ignored the law, and local strongmen sheltered fugitives.

sentences.zh: 祖深搜檢奸惡，不避強禦，動致刑辟。

translations.literal: Zushen searched out villainy, never avoiding the powerful, often bringing offenders to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zushen hunted down evildoers without flinching from the powerful, often sending them to execution.

sentences.zh: 奏江州刺史邵陵王、太子詹事周舍贓罪。

translations.literal: He memorialized the corrupt crimes of the Prince of Shaoling, Inspector of Jiang Province, and the Crown Prince's Household Steward Zhou She.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Prince Shaoling of Jiang Province and the Crown Prince's Household Steward Zhou She on charges of graft.

sentences.zh: 遠近側足，莫敢縱恣。

translations.literal: Near and far walked on tiptoe; none dared indulge themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, people walked on tiptoe; none dared misbehave.

sentences.zh: 淮南太守畏之如上府。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Huainan feared him as if he were a chief prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Huainan feared him as if he were a superior prefecture.

sentences.zh: 常服故布襦，素木案，食不過一肉。

translations.literal: He ordinarily wore old cotton short robes, used plain wooden desks, and ate no more than one dish of meat.
translations.idiomatic: He wore old cotton robes, used undecorated wooden desks, and never ate more than one meat dish at a meal.

sentences.zh: 有姥餉一早青瓜，祖深報以疋帛。

translations.literal: An old woman brought him a small early green melon; Zushen repaid her with a bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When an old woman brought him an early green melon, Zushen repaid her with a bolt of silk.

sentences.zh: 後有富人效之以貨，鞭而徇眾。

translations.literal: Later a rich man imitated this with goods; he was flogged and the act displayed to the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When a rich man tried the same trick with bribes, Zushen had him flogged and paraded before the public.

sentences.zh: 朝野憚之，絕於幹請。

translations.literal: Court and countryside feared him; private solicitations ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Officialdom and commoners alike feared him, and private solicitations ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 所領皆精兵，令行禁止。

translations.literal: Those under his command were all elite troops; orders were carried out and prohibitions enforced.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were all picked men; his orders ran and his prohibitions held.

sentences.zh: 有所討逐，越境追禽。

translations.literal: When pursuing and hunting criminals, he crossed borders to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit of fugitives he would cross borders to seize them.

sentences.zh: 江中嘗有賊，祖深自率討之，列陣未敢進，仍令所親人先登，不時進，斬之。

translations.literal: Once there were bandits on the river; Zushen personally led the attack; the battle line was formed but dared not advance, so he ordered a close follower to charge first; when he did not advance in time, Zushen beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits appeared on the river, Zushen led the attack himself; his line formed but hung back, so he ordered a trusted man to charge first—when the man failed to move in time, Zushen cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 遂大破賊，威振遠近，長江肅清。

translations.literal: He then routed the bandits; his authority shook far and near; the Yangzi was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the bandits; his authority resounded far and wide, and the Yangzi was cleared of crime.

sentences.zh: 論曰：善政之於人，猶良工之於埴也，用功寡而成器多焉。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Good government toward people is like a skilled craftsman toward clay—with little effort many vessels are formed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Good government among the people is like a master potter with his clay—a little effort yields many fine vessels.

sentences.zh: 漢世戶口殷盛，刑務簡闊，郡縣之職，外無橫擾，勸賞威刑，事多專斷，尺一詔書，希經邦邑。

translations.literal: In Han times household registers were abundant; penal affairs were simple and broad; the duties of commanderies and counties suffered no external harassment; encouragement, reward, awe, and punishment were mostly decided on their own; foot-long imperial edicts rarely passed through local seats.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the population was abundant and penal matters straightforward; commanderies and counties faced no outside interference; reward and punishment were largely their own to decide, and imperial edicts rarely reached down to local towns.

sentences.zh: 吏居官者或長子孫，皆敷德政以盡人和，興義讓以存簡久。

translations.literal: Officials in office sometimes lasted through sons and grandsons; all spread virtuous governance to achieve full human harmony, and raised righteousness and yielding to preserve simplicity for long.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials held office for generations; they spread benevolent rule to win hearts, and cultivated righteousness and deference to keep things simple and enduring.

sentences.zh: 故龔、黃之化，易以有成。

translations.literal: Therefore the transformations of Gong Yu and Huang Ba were easy to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the virtuous transformations of Gong Yu and Huang Ba were easily achieved.

sentences.zh: 降及晚代，情偽繁起，人減昔時，務殷前世。

translations.literal: Descending to late ages, cunning and falsity multiply; the population is less than before; official business is heavier than in earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: By later ages deceit proliferated, the population had shrunk, and official burdens weighed heavier than ever.

sentences.zh: 立績垂風，難易百倍。

translations.literal: To establish merit and leave a lasting model is a hundred times harder.
translations.idiomatic: To establish achievement and leave a lasting example was a hundred times harder.

sentences.zh: 若以上古之化，禦此世之人，今吏之良，撫前代之俗，則武城弦歌，將有未暇，淮陽臥鎮，如或可勉。

translations.literal: If ancient governance were applied to people of this age, or today's good officials were to soothe the customs of former ages—then the zither-songs of Wucheng would find no leisure, and Huaiyang's tranquil rule would be barely within reach.
translations.idiomatic: If the governance of antiquity were applied to people of this age—or today's best officials tried to govern the customs of former times—even the zither-songs of Wucheng would have no time to sound, and Huaiyang's quiet rule might barely be within reach.

sentences.zh: 未必今才陋古，蓋化有醇薄者也。

translations.literal: It is not necessarily that today's talent is baser than antiquity's; rather, the transformation itself has dense and thin phases.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that talent today is inferior to that of antiquity; rather, the temper of the age may be strong or weak.
